explanation: (D) ✓ — Per the Congress Ministries section: In Punjab, the Unionist Party under Sikandar Hayat Khan won the majority. ML1906 managed only 2 out of 175 seats in Punjab. With the Unionists in power, no Congress ministry was formed in Punjab.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Bihar was one of the six provinces where INC won an outright majority and formed a ministry.
(B) ✗ — Madras too was among the six INC-majority provinces of 1937 — a Congress ministry was formed there.
(C) ✗ — Orissa, a full province from 1936, was also among the six INC-majority provinces with a Congress ministry.
(Note: In Punjab, Sir Sikander Hyat Khan of National Unionist Party formed the government. Congress found absolute majority in five provinces.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.9
questions.stem: Which party was founded by Subhash Chandra Bose in the year 1939 after he broke away from the Congress?
explanation: (D) ✓ — The Forward Bloc: after the Tripuri clash with the Gandhian leadership, Bose resigned and formed it in 1939 as a left-wing faction to consolidate the Left inside the Congress.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — 'Indian Freedom Party' is a decoy name — no such party appears in these chapters; Bose's recorded 1939 formation is the Forward Bloc.
(B) ✗ — The Azad Hind Fauj (INA) was an army, not a political party — and it belongs to Bose's later war-time campaign abroad; the 1939 break from Congress produced the Forward Bloc.
(C) ✗ — 'Revolutionary Front' is a decoy; the organisation Bose founded in 1939 after breaking from the Congress is the Forward Bloc.

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.10
questions.stem: Consider the following statements The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for :
items: 1. the provincial autonomy.
2. the establishment of Federal court.
3. All India Federation at the centre.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: (D) ✓ — All three are recorded provisions: provincial autonomy — "all subjects in provinces became transferred subjects"; a Federal Court, actually set up in 1937; and a Federation of British India and the Princely States. Hence 1, 2 and 3.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Drops statement 3, but the All India Federation WAS provided for — it failed to materialise only because the Princes never signed the required Instruments of Accession.
(B) ✗ — Drops statement 1, but provincial autonomy is the Act's signature achievement — dyarchy ended and all provincial subjects came under popular ministers.
(C) ✗ — Drops statement 2, but the Federal Court is a recorded provision — established under the Act and set up in 1937, the ancestor of the Supreme Court.
(Note: The Government of India Act, 1935 was passed in August 1935. Some of the significant aspects of the act are : The grant of autonomy to the provinces of Bombay. Establishment of Federal court.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.11
questions.stem: Consider the following statements
items: 1. The discussions in the Third Round Table Conference eventually led to the passing of the Government of India Act of
2. The Government of India Act of 1935 provided for the establishment of an All India Federation to be based on a union of the provinces of British India and the Princely States.
questions.stemTail: 1935 Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
explanation: (C) ✓ — Both statements hold. Statement 1: the record legal-basis chain runs Simon Report → three RTCs → GOI Act 1935. Statement 2: India was to become a Union of British India & the Princely States with federal relations between the two.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Undercounts: statement 2 is also correct — the Act provided for a Federation uniting British India and the Princely States.
(B) ✗ — Undercounts the other way: statement 1 is also correct — the Act's lineage runs through the RTCs, the third of which closed the consultation chain.
(D) ✗ — Both statements are supported by the record — 'neither' cannot stand.

(Note: Main features of Government of India Act of 1935 are as under (i) Provision for the establishment of an All India Federation to be based on a union of the provinces of British India and the princely states.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.12
questions.stem: GOI Act 1935, residuary powers were given to:
explanation: (B) ✓ — point 4.6: The Viceroy retained residual powers, veto powers, ordinance powers, the power to restore cuts in grants, and the power to certify rejected bills. Residuary powers under GOI1935 vested in the Governor-General (Viceroy).
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — The Federal Legislature got no residuary powers — 80% of the central Budget was not even votable by it; the residual category sat with the Viceroy.
(C) ✗ — Provinces received constitutional ownership of the Provincial-list subjects only; residuary powers were retained by the Viceroy.
(D) ✗ — Provincial Governors held veto, ordinance, and take-over powers within their provinces — but the residuary category belonged to the Governor-General.

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.13
questions.stem: With reference to Indian National Movement, consider the following pairs. List I (Person) — List II (Position Held)
items: 1. Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru — President, All India Liberal Federation
2. KC Neogy — Member, Constituent Assembly
3. PC Joshi — General Secretary, Communist Party of India
questions.stemTail: Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
matchTable: General Secretary, Communist Party of India
explanation: (a) Only 1
(b) 1 and 2
(c) Only 3
(d) 1, 2 and 3

(D) ✓ — All three pairs hold: Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru founded and presided over the All India Liberal Federation (formed by Moderate leaders in 1919); K.C. Neogy sat in the Constituent Assembly; and P.C. Joshi served as General Secretary of CPI1925. Hence 1, 2 and 3.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Undercounts: pairs 2 and 3 are also correctly matched — K.C. Neogy (Constituent Assembly member) and P.C. Joshi (CPI General Secretary).
(B) ✗ — Drops pair 3, but P.C. Joshi's General-Secretaryship of CPI1925 is correctly matched.
(C) ✗ — Drops pair 1, but Sapru's presidency of the All India Liberal Federation is correctly matched.

(Note: Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru was the founder and President of All India Liberal Foundation. It was formed by the Moderate Congress Leaders in 1919. Its other leaders were Surendranath Banerjee, VS Srinivasa Sastri.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.14
questions.stem: Consider the following statements.
items: 1. The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 recommended granting voting rights to all the women above the age of 21.
2. The Government of India Act of 1935 gave women reserved seats in legislature.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: (B) ✓ — Statement 2 is recorded: GOI1935 gave women reserved seats through 'internal carve-outs' within each communal quota. Statement 1 fails: far from giving all women above 21 the vote in 1919, even under GOI1935 only about 10% of the population qualified, and a woman's right to vote was largely derived from her husband's income or property. Hence only 2.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Reverses the record: statement 1 is the false one — women's franchise stayed restricted and derived even in 1935 — while statement 2 (reserved seats for women) is true.
(C) ✗ — Statement 1 fails: no all-women-above-21 franchise existed — voting stayed tied to income, education, and (for women) the husband's status — so 'both' overcounts.
(D) ✗ — Statement 2 stands: "Reservation for women & labour/workers was also provided" — so 'neither' fails.

(Note: In the given Statements, (2) is correct. The Government of India Act, 1935 extended the principle of communal representation by providing separate electorates for depressed classes (scheduled castes).)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.15
questions.stem: With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935:
items: 1. Provided for All India Federation.
2. Defence/Foreign Affairs under federal legislature.
explanation: (A) ✓ — Statement 1 is recorded: India was to become a Union of British India & the Princely States. Statement 2 fails: Defence and External Affairs were among the four Reserved subjects under the absolute Legislative & Executive control of the Viceroy — not under the federal legislature. Hence 1 only.
Wrong options:
(B) ✗ — Exactly backwards: the Federation was provided for, while Defence and Foreign Affairs were Reserved to the Viceroy, outside the federal legislature's control.
(C) ✗ — Statement 2 fails — Defence and External Affairs sat in the Reserved list under the Viceroy's absolute control — so 'both' cannot stand.
(D) ✗ — Statement 1 stands — the All India Federation was a recorded provision of the Act — so 'neither' fails.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_1
questions.stem: Who was the Viceroy who actually implemented the GOI Act 1935 in 1937 and described the Act as "the best way to maintain control over India"?
explanation: Why others wrong: (a) Irwin preceded GOI 1935. (b) Willingdon's tenure ended before 1937 implementation. (d) Wavell came much later (1943 onward).
Memory hook: Linlithgow36-43 — the Viceroy who said the quiet part out loud.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_2
questions.stem: The Simon Commission Report (June 1930) recommended which of the following?
items: 1. Abolition of dyarchy in the provinces with full responsible provincial government
2. Introduction of responsible government at the Centre
3. Retention of separate electorates
4. Separation of Burma from India
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 2 is wrong: Simon recommended NO change at the Centre, which "remained under British despotism." Options (a), (b), (c) all retain statement 2.
Memory hook: Simon: yes to provinces, no to Centre — Burma packs its bags.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_3
questions.stem: With reference to the Three Round Table Conferences (1930-32), which one of the following statements is correct?

options.text: INC participated in all three RTCs.
The 2nd RTC accepted the Indian demand of Purna Swaraj.
The 3rd RTC was attended by both Gandhi and Jinnah.
The Princely States demanded a federation at the 1st RTC.

explanation: Why others wrong: (a) INC boycotted the 1st and 3rd RTCs; only the 2nd had INC. (b) Purna Swaraj and responsible government at the Centre were rejected at the 2nd RTC. (c) INC boycotted the 3rd RTC; participation was so low it was "practically irrelevant."
Memory hook: Princes at the 1st, Gandhi at the 2nd, nobody serious at the 3rd.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_4
questions.stem: Under the federal scheme of the GOI Act 1935, the minimum threshold of Princely States that had to sign the Instrument of Accession for the Federation to come into effect was:
explanation: Why others wrong: (a), (b), (c) — Section 6 of GOI1935 required at least 50% of Princes to sign the IoA; that threshold was never met, so the Federation never came into effect.
Memory hook: Fifty per cent — and the Princes simply refused to dance.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_5
questions.stem: Under the GOI Act 1935, a Princely State signing the Instrument of Accession would transfer which subjects to the Union Government?
items: 1. Defence
2. Foreign Affairs
3. Finance
4. Communications
explanation: Why others wrong: Finance was NOT one of the three. The record states only Defence, Foreign Affairs and Communications were to go to the Union — structurally identical to how J&K signed only an IoA in 1947. Options containing "3" are wrong.
Memory hook: Three keys to the Union: Defence, Foreign, Comms — the Art. 370 ancestor.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_6
questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the proposed bicameral central legislature under the GOI Act 1935:
items: 1. One-third of the Federal Assembly members were to be nominees of the Princes.
2. Elections to the Federal Assembly were to be direct, and those to the Council of States indirect.
3. The Council of States was to be a permanent house with one-third of its members retiring every third year.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 2 reverses the truth: FA elections were INDIRECT (to limit INC) and CoS elections were DIRECT. Options (a), (b), (c) all retain the reversed statement.
Memory hook: FA = indirect (kill INC), CoS = direct, permanent — Princes pad the FA.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_7
questions.stem: Under the GOI Act 1935, the four subjects classified as "Reserved" under the proposed dyarchy at the Centre were:

options.text: Defence, Home, Ecclesiastical Affairs, Tribal Areas
Defence, External Affairs, Ecclesiastical Affairs, Tribal Areas
Defence, External Affairs, Finance, Tribal Areas

explanation: Why others wrong: the record explicitly warns that Finance and Home were legally TRANSFERRED subjects, not Reserved. Options (a), (b), (d) all wrongly include Finance or Home among the Reserved Four.
Memory hook: Reserved 4 = Defence, External, Ecclesiastical, Tribal — Finance is a trap.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_8
questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the franchise under the GOI Act 1935:
items: 1. Only about 10% of the population qualified to vote.
2. A woman could vote based on her husband's income or property, with a lower financial threshold than that required for men.
3. Universal Adult Franchise was introduced for the first time.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 3 is wrong: UAF was a consistent INC demand from 1928 onwards but was NOT granted by GOI 1935; the Act gave only ~10% the vote. (b), (c), (d) all retain statement 3.
Memory hook: 10% with vote, wives derived from husbands — UAF still a dream.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_9
questions.stem: Which one of the following was introduced for the first time under the GOI Act 1935 in respect of the Scheduled Castes/Depressed Classes?

options.text: Separate electorates exclusively for Depressed Classes.
Reservation in nominated seats in the central legislature.
Reservation in elected seats with Joint Electorates in the FA, CoS and PLAs.
Complete abolition of caste-based reservation in legislatures.

explanation: Why others wrong: (a) The Communal Award proposed separate electorates for Depressed Classes but Poona Pact converted this to joint electorates with reserved seats; this is what GOI 1935 implemented. (b) Reservation in NOMINATED seats was under GOI 1919; 1935 upgraded it to ELECTED. (d) No abolition — GOI 1935 expanded representation.
Memory hook: 1919: nominated; 1935: ELECTED reserved seats — step forward for SCs.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_10
questions.stem:
Match List I (Institution/Provision) with List II (Year of operation/effect under GOI 1935 framework):

List I
A. Federal Court actually set up
B. Reserve Bank of India became operational
C. Burma separated from India
D. NWFP gained full responsible government

List II
items: 1. 1 April 1935
matchTable: List II (List II (Year of operation/effect under GOI 1935 framework))
Reserve Bank of India became operational
explanation: Why others wrong: Only RBI was operational from 1 April 1935 (under RBI Act 1934). Federal Court, Burma separation and NWFP full responsible government all date to 1937. Options (a), (c), (d) misalign RBI's 1935 date.
Memory hook: RBI alone is 1935; everything else waits for 1937.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_11
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Governor's powers in the provinces under the GOI Act 1935:
items: 1. 40% of the provincial Budget was non-votable.
2. The Governor had the power to take over the government and run it indefinitely.
3. The Governor lost his power to issue ordinances.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 3 is wrong: the Governor retained ordinance power (and veto, summoning, special powers, etc.). Options (b), (c), (d) all retain statement 3. The record lists "take over the government" power as the ancestor of Art. 356.
Memory hook: 40% non-votable + Art. 356 ancestor — Governor still hovers.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_12
questions.stem: Arrange the following constitutional/administrative events in correct chronological order:
items: 1. Carving of NWFP as a Chief Commissioner's Province
2. Raising of NWFP to Governor's Province
3. Separation of Sindh from Bombay
4. Separation of Burma from India
explanation: Why others wrong: Order per Chapter: NWFP CC province 1901 → NWFP Governor's Province 1932 → Sindh separated 1936 → Burma separated 1937. Options (b), (c), (d) misorder these dates.
Memory hook: 1901 → 1932 → 1936 → 1937 — North-West first, Burma last.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_13
questions.stem: With reference to fiscal autonomy under the GOI Act 1935, which one of the following is correct?

options.text: Financial control over British India was transferred from the Viceroy to the Secretary of State for India.
Financial control over British India was transferred from the Secretary of State for India in London to the Viceroy in India.
Financial control was vested for the first time in an elected Indian Finance Member.
The Secretary of State for India was abolished by the Act.

explanation: Why others wrong: (a) Reverses the direction. (c) No such Indian Finance Member with full fiscal autonomy — Viceroy retained certifying powers and 80% non-votable Budget. (d) SoSforIndia continued until 1947. Nehru called this "the only major change" in the entire Act.
Memory hook: London loses the purse — Viceroy in Delhi now holds it.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_14
questions.stem: Under the GOI Act 1935, the federal distribution of subjects was made into three lists. Which one of the following correctly names those three lists?
explanation: Why others wrong: (a) "Union/State" is the COI 1950 terminology — the 7th Schedule descendant. (b) and (d) are fabricated combinations not used by GOI 1935.
Memory hook: Federal-Concurrent-Provincial — the grandparent of the 7th Schedule.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_15
questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the 1937 provincial elections and Congress Ministries:
items: 1. INC won a majority in 6 provinces and formed ministries in 8 out of 11 provinces.
2. In Punjab, the Muslim League won a sweeping majority.
3. In Bengal, Assam and NWFP, INC emerged as the largest party without a majority.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 2 is wrong: in Punjab, the Unionist Party under Sikandar Hayat Khan won; ML1906 managed only 2 of 175 seats. Options (a), (c), (d) retain statement 2.
Memory hook: 6 majority + 8 ministries — and Sikandar Hayat, not Jinnah, ruled Punjab.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_16
questions.stem: The evolution of Muslim voting rights from 1909 to 1919 is best described as a shift from:

options.text: the "Double Vote" to watertight separate rolls with cross-voting strictly banned.
reserved seats with joint electorates to separate electorates.
universal adult franchise to communal franchise.

explanation: Why others wrong: (a) 1909 already introduced separate electorates — not joint. (c) Joint electorates with reserved seats came for SCs in 1935, not for Muslims in 1909-19. (d) UAF never existed in either Act.
Memory hook: 1909 = Double Vote; 1919 (Lucknow Pact echo) = watertight rolls.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_17
questions.stem: Arrange the following Acts in correct chronological order according to when each first introduced the feature shown alongside:
items: 1. First real elections (indirect for general seats; direct for Muslim seats) — ICA 1909
2. First non-official majority in Provincial Legislative Councils — ICA 1909
3. First direct elections for the CLA, CoS and PLAs — GOI 1919
4. First proper federal distribution of subjects into three lists — GOI 1935
explanation: Why others wrong: Per: ICA 1909 introduced both first real elections AND first non-official majority in PLCs (in that listed order in -8.3); GOI 1919 introduced first direct elections for CLA/CoS/PLAs; GOI 1935 introduced the proper federal distribution. Other orderings misplace 1909's twin firsts or push 1919 ahead of 1909 features.
Memory hook: 1909 — elections + PLC non-official majority; 1919 — direct elections; 1935 — federal lists.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_18
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about the non-votable portion of the Budget across British constitutional Acts is correct?

options.text: Under GOI 1919, 80% of the Budget was non-votable at the Centre.
Under GOI 1935, 80% of the central and 40% of the provincial Budget were non-votable.
Under ICA 1909, the entire Budget became votable for the first time.
Under GOI 1935, the entire central Budget became votable.

explanation: (b) ✓ — [, Democracy & Legislature Power + ]
Why others wrong: (a) Under GOI 1919, 75% of the Budget was non-votable, not 80%. (c) ICA 1909 only allowed vote on items (not whole). (d) GOI 1935 still kept 80% of central Budget non-votable.
Memory hook: 75 → 80 at Centre; 40 in province — Viceroy's iron grip on rupees.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_19
questions.stem:
Match List I (Reason the Princely States refused to sign the Instrument of Accession) with List II (Specific concern):

List I
A. Paramountcy not abolished
B. Financial autonomy at stake
C. Smaller States' worry
D. Fear of democracy

List II
items: 1. Low representation at the Centre in proposed legislatures
2. INC could launch movements inside the States after Union
3. Two bosses — Union Government and British Crown
4. GOI could compel Princes to contribute to Defence Budget
matchTable: List I (List I (Reason the Princely States refused to sign the Instrument of Accession))
Low representation at the Centre in proposed legislatures
INC could launch movements inside the States after Union
Two bosses — Union Government and British Crown
GOI could compel Princes to contribute to Defence Budget
explanation: Why others wrong: Per: Paramountcy → "two bosses" (3); Financial autonomy → forced Defence Budget contribution (4); Smaller States → low Centre representation (1); Fear of democracy → INC movements inside States (2). Other options scramble these pairings.
Memory hook: Two bosses, forced cheque, fewer seats, democratic invasion — four reasons the Princes stayed out.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_20
questions.stem: With reference to the impact of the Congress Ministries of 1937-39, consider the following statements:
items: 1. The Ministries energised people in the Princely States through new and expanded Praja Mandals (State People's Congresses).
2. The Narendra Mandal or Chamber of Princes was set up in 1921 as a popular response from below to the Princely States question.
3. INC gained crucial administrative and governance experience during this 28-month period.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 2 is wrong: the Narendra Mandal (1921) was the British RESPONSE FROM ABOVE — an advisory body of Princely States to the British. The Congress ministries energised the popular response FROM BELOW. Options (a), (b), (d) retain statement 2.
Memory hook: Praja Mandals from below (1937-39); Chamber of Princes from above (1921).

questions.label: FYQ_M.1
questions.stem: The Federation proposed under GOI 1935 was the most ambitious constitutional construction of British rule in India — yet it never came into effect. Examine why.
body: Demand of the question: "Examine why it never came into effect" requires tracing both the structural design flaw & the contingent failures.

Suggested intro (~25 words): GOI 1935 proposed a federal structure linking British India provinces with Princely States — an unprecedented constitutional architecture. By 1939, it had collapsed without ever operating.
Body guidance — 4 themes:

1. The structural prerequisite (see 'Features at the Centre — The Part That Never Happened'). Federation required Princely States representing at least 50% of total population & at least 50% of available seats in the Federal Legislature to accede. The British made this voluntary, anticipating gradual accession.

2. The Princely refusal (see 'Features at the Centre — The Part That Never Happened'). Most Princes saw the Federation framework as a threat to their internal sovereignty — the Federal Legislature could legislate on matters they had previously decided autonomously. By 1939, fewer than 14 small Princely States had acceded; the population threshold was nowhere near met.

3. The Congress critique (see 'Features at the Provinces — The Part That Did Work (from 1937)'). Congress rejected Federation on different grounds — it gave Princely States disproportionate representation in the Federal Legislature (more seats per population than democratically elected British India provinces). Nehru called the Princes "feudal autocrats" being given veto over democratic India.

4. WWII & the closure (see 'Features at the Centre — The Part That Never Happened'). September 1939 — WWII began. Britain quietly shelved Federation work. The provincial autonomy provisions continued operating, but the Centre stayed under the GOI 1919 framework (modified) for the rest of British rule. Federation was de facto cancelled in 1939, de jure never revived.

Closing verdict: GOI 1935's Federation failed not because it was poorly designed, but because the constituents the British wanted to include (Princes) had veto power over their own inclusion & refused to use it. The principle of voluntary accession ensured an inability to ever assemble a federation. The lesson — that voluntary federation between feudal & democratic units cannot work — shaped the 1947 integration approach (Patel + Menon's Standstill + Instrument of Accession framework).

questions.label: FYQ_M.2
questions.stem: The Congress Ministries (1937-39) under GOI 1935 were the first taste of self-government for Indian leaders. Examine what they achieved & why they resigned in October 1939.
body: Demand of the question: "Examine what achieved & why resigned" demands both halves.
Suggested intro (~25 words): Congress Ministries governed 8 of 11 provinces from April 1937 to October 1939 — the first sustained Indian-led government experience. They resigned over WWII.
Body guidance — 3 themes (see 'Features at the Provinces — The Part That Did Work (from 1937)'):

1. Achievements. Legislative reforms: tenancy reforms favouring peasants, mass education expansion, prohibition policies in Madras & Bombay, labour welfare measures, release of political prisoners. Administrative experience: Congress cadres learned governance — Patel, Rajagopalachari, B.G. Kher emerged as ministerial leaders.

2. The Constraints. Governors retained reserve powers (could veto, dissolve, appoint ministers under exceptional circumstances). The Federation never came into effect at the Centre — so Congress provinces operated without a federal Indian government above them; the Centre stayed under the Governor-General.

3. The Resignation (October 1939). Viceroy Linlithgow declared India a co-belligerent in WWII (September 1939) WITHOUT consulting Congress provinces. Congress demanded a clear post-war commitment to independence — refused. All Congress Ministries resigned in protest October-November 1939. The British declared "President's Rule" via Governors.

Closing verdict: The Ministries proved Indian capacity for self-government — but also revealed that genuine self-rule required ending the Viceroy's reserve powers entirely. The 1939 resignation set the stage for Quit India 1942.

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.1
questions.stem: Assertion [A] The Congress rejected the cripps proposals. Reason [R] The Cripps Mission consisted solely of whites.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: (B) ✓ — Both parts are true: INC did reject the proposals — wanting Purna Swaraj, not Dominion Status — and the Mission was an all-British team: Cripps plus "senior British officials". But the composition was not the reason for rejection — the recorded grounds were Dominion Status instead of Purna Swaraj, the Princes' nominees in the Constituent Assembly, and the right to secede. Hence R is true but does not explain A.
Wrong options:

(A) ✗ — Fails on the explanation test: the recorded rejection grounds are constitutional — Dominion Status, secession rights, unelected Princely-State nominees — not the Mission's all-British composition.
(C) ✗ — R is not false: the Mission was led by Cripps with "senior British officials" as the other members — no Indian on the team.
(D) ✗ — A is not false: INC rejected the offer — MG dismissed it as a "post-dated cheque".

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.2
questions.stem: Which Indian nationalist leader looked upon a war between Germany and Britain as a godsent opportunity which would enable Indians to exploit the situation to their advantage?
explanation: (C) ✓ — Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose took the opposite view. Britain's weakness was India's opportunity, and the moment called for an immediate Civil Disobedience Movement. That is precisely the 'godsent opportunity' position.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — No such view is recorded for Rajagopalachari; the opportunity-seizing position belongs to Bose alone — most INC leaders privately favoured an Allied victory.

(B) ✗ — Jinnah's recorded wartime opportunity was political, not military: ML1906 used INC's confrontation with the British to pass the Lahore Resolution demanding Pakistan in March 1940. The war-as-opportunity stance is Bose's.
(D) ✗ — Nehru's recorded position was the opposite of adventurism: no cooperation without Purna Swaraj, but also "no mass movement during the war itself".

(Note: The deteriorate condition of Europe during the Second World War made many advocated to involved in colonial India, the sense of complete freedom. Subhash Chandra Bose was eager to take advantage of hostilities.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.3
questions.stem: An important aspect of the Cripps Mission of 1942 was

options.text: that all Indian states should join the Indian union as a condition to consider any degree of autonomy for India
the creation of an Indian Union with dominion status very soon after the Second World War

the active participation and cooperation of the Indian people, communities and political parties in the British war efforts as a condition for granting independence with full sovereign status to India after war
the framing of a Constitution for the entire Indian union, with no separate Constitution for any province and a Union Constitution to be accepted by all provinces

explanation: (B) ✓ — Provisions: (@Swaraj) Dominion Status after the war, plus Indian control over foreign policy. An Indian Union with Dominion Status soon after the war was the heart of the offer.
Wrong options:

(A) ✗ — Reversed: far from making accession compulsory, the offer's most explosive provision allowed any Province or Princely State that disagreed with the new constitution NOT to join the Union and to frame its own constitution.
(C) ✗ — Full sovereign status was never on the table: the offer stopped at Dominion Status — "still Dominion Status, not Purna Swaraj".
(D) ✗ — Reversed again: instead of one constitution binding all provinces, a dissenting Province or State could refuse the framed constitution and write its own — the 576-entities danger.
(Note: An important aspect of Cripps Mission, under the leadership of Stafford Cripps was the creation of Indian union with dominion status, very soon after the war.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.4
questions.stem: Assertion (A) The Congress Ministries in all the provinces resigned in the year 1939. Reason (R) The Congress did not accept the decision of the Viceroy to declare war against Germany in the context of the II World War. Codes

options.text: A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
A and R are individually true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: (A) ✓ — Both Assertion and Reason are true, and R IS the correct explanation of A. Viceroy Linlithgow declared India a co-belligerent in WWII (Sept 1939) without consulting Indian leaders. The Congress Working Committee at the Wardha Meet (Sept-Oct 1939) directed all Congress-led provincial ministries to resign in protest. The resignation (Assertion) was directly caused by Congress's refusal to accept the unilateral war declaration (Reason).
Wrong options:

(B) ✗ — The explanation IS direct: the Viceroy's unilateral war declaration led straight to the Wardha directive that "Congress ministries in the Provinces were directed to resign". R correctly explains A.
(C) ✗ — R is not false: Britain declared India a belligerent "without consent" and the CWC refused to support the war effort.
(D) ✗ — A is not false: the resignation of the Congress ministries is recorded — it "shook the British" into making the August Offer.

(Note: Indian Viceroy Lord Linlithgow declared India against Germany in II World War dated 17th October, 1939. The Indian National Congress Working Committee on 23rd October, 1939, decided not to support the war effort.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.5
questions.stem: In the 'Individual Satyagraha', Vinoba Bhave was chosen as the first Satyagrahi. Who was the second?
explanation: (B) ✓ — The first three Satyagrahis were Vinobha Bhave, Nehru, and Brahma Dutt — arrested in that order. Nehru was the second Satyagrahi.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Rajendra Prasad does not figure in the recorded sequence — Vinobha Bhave, then Nehru, then Brahma Dutt.
(C) ✗ — Rajagopalachari is not in the recorded trio of first Satyagrahis; the second place is Nehru's.
(D) ✗ — Patel has no recorded role in the Individual Satyagraha sequence; the order ran Bhave → Nehru → Brahma Dutt.
(Note: Gandhiji initiated a limited Satyagraha on individual basis in every locality. The Gandhiji chosen satyagrahis would preach against participation in the war.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.6
questions.stem: Consider the following statements The Cripps proposals include the provision for
items: 1. full independence for India.
2. creation of Constitution making body. 3.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
explanation: (B) ✓ — Statement 2 is recorded: a post-war Constituent Assembly "composed solely of Indians" was a Cripps provision. Statement 1 fails: the offer was Dominion Status, "not Purna Swaraj". Hence only 2.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Exactly reversed: no full independence was offered (Dominion Status only), while a Constitution-making body WAS provided.
(C) ✗ — Statement 1 fails — the offer's @Swaraj verdict's own summary reads "Failed: Only Dominion Status offered, not Purna Swaraj" — so 'both' overcounts.
(D) ✗ — Statement 2 stands: the Constituent Assembly provision is recorded — so 'neither' fails.
(Note: In 1942, the British Government realised that the Indian problems cannot be ignored any more. As a result of the World War the situation worsened for British with Japanese advance.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.7
questions.stem: Who of the following Prime Ministers sent Cripps Mission to India?
explanation: (D) ✓ — Background: Britain sent the Cripps Mission in March 1942, led by Sir Stafford Cripps, a minister in the War Cabinet of Prime Minister Winston Churchill.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Ramsay MacDonald's recorded India landmark is the Communal Award of August 1932 — a decade before the Cripps Mission; the 1942 War Cabinet was Churchill's.
(B) ✗ — Stanley Baldwin has no recorded India role in these chapters; the Mission's despatching PM is named — Winston Churchill.
(C) ✗ — Chamberlain's premiership belonged to the war's outbreak phase; by March 1942 Cripps was a minister in the War Cabinet of Prime Minister Winston Churchill.

(Note: Winston Churchill, the Prime Minister of England, sent Cripps Mission to India. Winston Churchill announced on 11th March, 1942 that the British Cabinet was sending a mission to India under Sir Stafford Cripps.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.8
questions.stem: Who among the following were official Congress negotiators with Cripps Mission?

options.text: Acharya J B Kripalani and C Rajagopalachari
Dr Rajendra Prasad and Rafi Ahmed Kidwai

explanation: (C) ✓ — Nehru and Maulana Azad. Azad was the INC's serving President through the war years, and Nehru was the leader most invested in a negotiated path — INC's December 1941 offer of war support had been made "overriding the individual objections of both Nehru & MG", and his stated line was negotiation without a wartime mass movement. They negotiated for the party with Cripps.
Wrong options:

(A) ✗ — MG stood apart from the negotiation: the December 1941 decision to engage had overridden his objections, and his verdict on the offer — a "post-dated cheque" — was that of a critic, not an official negotiator.
(B) ✗ — Neither Kripalani nor Rajagopalachari is recorded as negotiating with Cripps; the negotiating pair credited in this Answer Key is Nehru and Azad (see the ✓ entry above).
(D) ✗ — Rajendra Prasad and Rafi Ahmed Kidwai have no recorded role in the Cripps talks; the official pair was Nehru and Azad (see the ✓ entry above).

(Note: The Cripps Mission was an attempt in late March, 1942 by the British Government to secure Indian cooperation and support for their efforts in World War II. The Mission was headed by Sir Stafford Cripps.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.9
questions.stem: The Congress ministries resigned in the seven provinces in 1939, because

options.text: the Congress could not form ministries in the other four provinces
emergence of a left wing in the Congress made the working of the ministries impossible
there were widespread communal disturbances in their provinces
None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given above is correct

explanation: (D) ✓ — None of the three listed reasons is the recorded one: the ministries resigned because Linlithgow36-43 declared India a belligerent "without consent" and the Wardha Meet of the CWC then directed them to resign. Hence (d).
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — INC had actually formed ministries in 8 of 11 provinces in 1937; the 1939 exit was a war-protest directive, not a ministry-formation problem.
(B) ✗ — The Left's drama — Tripuri and the Forward Bloc — was an internal party affair; the ministries' recorded exit cause was the CWC's Wardha directive over the unconsulted war declaration.
(C) ✗ — No communal-disturbance cause is recorded; the resignations followed the CWC's Wardha decision in protest at Britain dragging India into the war without consultation.

(Note: The Congress ministries resigned on 22nd December, 1939; in the wake of II World War as the Viceroy unilaterally included India with the declaration of war on Germany without consulting any Indian leaders.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.10
questions.stem: The plan of Sir Stafford Cripps envisaged that after the Second World War

options.text: India should be granted complete Independence.
India should be partitioned into two before granting Independence.
India should be made a Republic with the condition that she will join the Commonwealth.
India should be given Dominion status.

explanation: (D) ✓ — Provisions: (@Swaraj) Dominion Status after the war, plus Indian control over foreign policy. (... it was still Dominion Status, not Purna Swaraj.) Dominion Status after the war is what the Cripps plan envisaged.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Complete independence was never offered — the record own summary of the offer reads @Swaraj — Failed: Only Dominion Status offered, not Purna Swaraj.

(B) ✗ — No two-way partition was proposed: the danger was the secession option that could crumble India into as many as 576 entities — and ML1906 opposed the offer precisely because it did NOT provide two Constituent Assemblies.
(C) ✗ — A Republic was never on offer: Dominion Status "keeps India tethered within the British Empire" — the very opposite of a sovereign republic.

(Note: In March 1942, a Mission headed by Stafford Cripps was sent to India with constitutional proposals to seek Indian support for the Second World War. Sir Stafford Cripps was a senior left-wing politician.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.11
questions.stem: Proposals of Cripps Mission:
items: 1. Constituent Assembly with nominated members.
2. Provinces right to separate agreement.
explanation: (B) ✓ — Statement 2 is recorded: a Province that did not accept the framed constitution could stay out of the Union and frame its own constitution or set up its own union within the British Empire — i.e. a separate arrangement with Britain. Statement 1 fails: provincial members of the Constituent Assembly were to be ELECTED from the PLAs — only the Princely States sent unelected nominees. Hence 2 only.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Reversed: statement 1 is the flawed one — PLA members were elected, not nominated — while statement 2 is the recorded secession option.
(C) ✗ — Statement 1 fails on the word 'nominated': only Princely-State representatives were nominees; provincial members came by election from the PLAs.
(D) ✗ — Statement 2 stands: the right of a dissenting Province to stay out and frame its own arrangement is recorded — so 'neither' fails.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_1
questions.stem: When Britain declared war on Germany in September 1939, who was the Viceroy who declared India a belligerent without consulting Indian leaders?
explanation: (b) ✓ Linlithgow36-43 (1936–43) was Viceroy when Britain declared war and did not bother to consult Indian leaders.
Why others wrong: (a) Willingdon's tenure ended 1936, before WW II; (c) Wavell came later (1943–47); (d) Wellesley belongs to early 19th-century, irrelevant to WW II.
Memory hook: Linlithgow signed India into a war it never agreed to fight.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_2
questions.stem: Who defeated Mahatma Gandhi's preferred candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya in the INC presidential election at the Tripuri Session (1939)?
explanation: (c) ✓ Bose defeated Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Tripuri 1939, prompting Gandhi's "Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat" remark.

Why others wrong: (a) Nehru was not the rival candidate at Tripuri; (b) Azad held the presidency in later sessions, not as Gandhi's rival here; (d) Patel was aligned with the Gandhi-led leadership, not its challenger.
Memory hook: Tripuri 1939: Bose wins the chair, Gandhi calls it his own defeat.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_3
questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the 1939 Wardha Meet of the Congress Working Committee (CWC):
items: 1. The INC refused to support the British war effort.
2. Congress ministries in the Provinces were directed to resign.
3. Linlithgow responded by promising Purna Swaraj after the war.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: (a) ✓ At Wardha the CWC refused to support the war effort and directed Congress ministries to resign. Statement 3 is wrong — Linlithgow panicked and promised only Dominion Status (not Purna Swaraj) after the war.

Why others wrong: (b), (c), (d) all include statement 3, which is factually wrong — the post-Wardha British promise was Dominion Status, the same "old wine, new bottle" already offered by Irwin in 1929.
Memory hook: Wardha 1939: refuse war + resign ministries. Britain offers Dominion Status, not Purna Swaraj.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_4
questions.stem: With reference to the August Offer (1940) by Linlithgow, consider the following statements:
items: 1. It promised a Constituent Assembly after the war where mainly Indians would frame the constitution.
2. It promised Purna Swaraj after the war.
3. It included a clause that no future constitution would be framed without the consent of minorities.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: (b) ✓ AO1940 promised a post-war Constituent Assembly "mainly" of Indians and the "no future constitution without the consent of minorities" clause that gave ML1906 a veto. Statement 2 is wrong — the offer was Dominion Status after the war, not Purna Swaraj.
Why others wrong: (a) and (d) include the wrong Purna Swaraj claim; (c) drops the correct Constituent Assembly clause and retains the Purna Swaraj error.
Memory hook: August 1940: mainly-Indian CA, minority veto, Dominion Status — never Purna Swaraj.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_5
questions.stem: Under the August Offer (1940), which of the following was the position regarding the Viceroy's Executive Council (VEC)?

options.text: The VEC was to be abolished and replaced by an Indian Council of Ministers
The VEC was to be retained without any change in composition
The VEC was to be expanded to include more Indians
The VEC was to be transferred entirely to ministers nominated by the INC

explanation: (c) ✓ The August Offer promised that the Viceroy's Executive Council (VEC) would be expanded to include more Indians, building on the GOI Act 1919 baseline of 3 Indian members out of 8.

Why others wrong: (a) The Viceroy and the VEC were retained, not abolished; (b) the whole point of AO1940 was expansion of the VEC, not status-quo; (d) no INC nomination right was granted under the August Offer.
Memory hook: August Offer = bigger VEC, not a new Cabinet.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_6
questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the form of protest under Individual Satyagraha launched by Mahatma Gandhi in October 1940?

options.text: A no-tax campaign in the Provinces against revenue collection
A public anti-war speech asserting the right to freedom of speech
A mass picketing of liquor shops and foreign-cloth stores
Surrender of titles conferred by the British Government

explanation: (b) ✓ The Satyagrahi was to make a public anti-war speech and assert the right to freedom of speech — a deliberate, narrow, symbolic protest, not a mass Civil Disobedience Movement.

Why others wrong: (a) No-tax campaigns were associated with earlier movements like Bardoli, not Individual Satyagraha; (c) mass picketing was a CDM 1930 feature, not the Individual Satyagraha form; (d) surrender of titles belongs to NCM 1920–22, not 1940.
Memory hook: October 1940: one Satyagrahi, one anti-war speech, one freedom-of-speech claim.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_7
questions.stem: Consider the following pairs regarding Individual Satyagraha (1940):
items: 1. First Satyagrahi : Vinobha Bhave
2. Second Satyagrahi : Brahma Dutt
3. Third Satyagrahi : Jawaharlal Nehru
questions.stemTail: Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
explanation: (a) ✓ The first three Satyagrahis, arrested in order under the Defence of India Act 1939, were Vinobha Bhave, Nehru, and Brahma Dutt. So Vinobha Bhave (first) is correctly paired; Nehru was second (not third) and Brahma Dutt was third (not second).
Why others wrong: (b) Pair 2 reverses Nehru and Brahma Dutt's order; (c) Pair 3 wrongly puts Nehru third; (d) includes both incorrect pairs.
Memory hook: Vinobha-Nehru-Brahma Dutt — Satyagraha trio in arrest-order.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_8
questions.stem: Under which Act were the first Satyagrahis arrested during Individual Satyagraha in 1940?
explanation: (c) ✓ Individual Satyagraha was directed against the Defence of India Act, 1939 — an emergency law restricting civil liberties during wartime — and the first three Satyagrahis were arrested under this Act.

Why others wrong: (a) The 1915 Act applied to WW I emergency, not WW II; (b) the Rowlatt Act 1919 was the trigger for earlier anti-war repression but was not the law used in 1940 arrests; (d) GOI 1935 framed the constitutional set-up, not the wartime emergency arrests.
Memory hook: DIA 1939 — the wartime gag that Individual Satyagraha was designed to break.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_9
questions.stem: Regarding the 1941 expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council (VEC), consider the following statements:
items: 1. The number of Indians in the VEC rose from 3 out of 8 members to 8 out of 12 members.
2. For the first time, Indian ministers were in a majority at the Centre.
3. The portfolios of Defence, Home, and Finance were transferred to Indian ministers.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: (a) ✓ The 1941 expansion took Indian members from 3/8 to 8/12 (statement 1) and gave Indians a majority at the Centre for the first time (statement 2). Statement 3 is wrong — Defence, Home, and Finance were explicitly NOT to be held by Indian ministers.
Why others wrong: (b), (c), (d) all include statement 3, but the three "portfolios that mattered most" remained outside Indian ministers' reach in 1941.
Memory hook: 1941: Indian majority on paper, but Defence-Home-Finance still British.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_10
questions.stem: Sir Stafford Cripps, who led the Cripps Mission to India in March 1942, was:

options.text: A minister in the War Cabinet of Prime Minister Winston Churchill
The Secretary of State for India in the Atlee Government

explanation: (b) ✓ Britain sent the Cripps Mission in March 1942, led by Sir Stafford Cripps, a minister in the War Cabinet of Prime Minister Winston Churchill, with senior British officials as other members.
Why others wrong: (a) No such post sent Cripps; (c) Atlee became PM only in 1945 — Churchill was PM in 1942; (d) Cripps was a politician-minister, not the Commander-in-Chief.
Memory hook: Cripps 1942 — Churchill's War Cabinet minister, not a soldier.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_11
questions.stem: Arrange the following WW II-era events in correct chronological order:
items: 1. Wardha Meet of the CWC — refusal to support war
2. Lahore Resolution of the Muslim League demanding Pakistan
3. Launch of Individual Satyagraha by Gandhi
4. Cripps Mission to India
explanation: (d) ✓ — [;; ] Wardha CWC = 1939 → Lahore Resolution = March 1940 → Individual Satyagraha = October 1940 → Cripps Mission = March 1942.

Why others wrong: (a), (c) wrongly place the Lahore Resolution before the Wardha Meet — Wardha 1939 came first and ML's Lahore Resolution was a March 1940 response; (b) wrongly puts Individual Satyagraha (Oct 1940) before the Lahore Resolution (March 1940).
Memory hook: Wardha → Lahore → Individual Satyagraha → Cripps. Refuse, demand, protest, parley.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_12
questions.stem:
Match List I with List II:
| List I (Year) | List II (Event) |
|---|---|
| A. 1939 |
items:
1. August Offer by Linlithgow |
| B. 1940 |

2. Cripps Mission |
| C. 1941 |

3. Wardha Meet of the CWC |
| D. 1942 |
4. Expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council |
matchTable: Expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council
explanation: (a) ✓ — [;;; ] 1939 → Wardha CWC (refusal to support war); 1940 → August Offer; 1941 → VEC expanded to 8/12 Indians; 1942 → Cripps Mission.
Why others wrong: (b) misplaces August Offer at 1939; (c) swaps the VEC expansion to 1940; (d) puts Cripps in 1939 and Wardha in 1942 — both calendar-wrong.
Memory hook: 39 Wardha, 40 August, 41 VEC, 42 Cripps.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_13
questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Cripps Mission (1942):
items: 1. It offered Dominion Status after the war, plus Indian control over Defence.
2. The Constituent Assembly was to be composed solely of Indians.
3. Any Province of British India or Princely State that disagreed with the framed constitution could opt not to join the Union.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: (b) ✓ — (b) ✓ Statements 2 and 3 are core provisions of the Cripps offer: a Constituent Assembly composed solely of Indians (an upgrade over AO1940's "mainly" Indians), and the explosive secession option for any dissenting Province or Princely State — opening the path to 565 + 11 = 576 possible entities. Statement 1 misplaces the portfolio: Cripps added Indian control over foreign policy to Dominion Status, but Defence was expressly to remain with the Viceroy during the war — and it was on exactly that point that the talks broke down.

Why others wrong: (a) 1 and 2 only — carries statement 1, which hands Defence to Indians; under Cripps, Defence stayed with the Viceroy, and the Indian gain was foreign policy. (c) 1 and 3 only — same defect: "Indian control over Defence" contradicts the Viceroy's retention of Defence, the very sticking point that killed the negotiations. (d) 1, 2 and 3 — cannot stand once statement 1 is false; the tempting all-inclusive option is the trap here.
Memory hook: Cripps = Dominion Status + foreign affairs to Indians, Defence to the Viceroy + solely-Indian CA + right to secede.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_14
questions.stem: Mahatma Gandhi famously described the Cripps offer (1942) as:

options.text: Old wine in a new bottle
An empty gesture from a bankrupt empire

explanation: (c) ✓ Gandhi called the Cripps offer a "post-dated cheque" — most things were to take effect after the war, and nothing was immediate.

Why others wrong: (a) "Leap in the dark" was Robert Lowe's tag for the 1867 British Reform Act, not Gandhi's tag for Cripps; (b) "old wine, new bottle" describes Linlithgow's 1939 Dominion-Status promise mirroring Irwin's 1929 promise, not of Cripps; (d) is not Gandhi's recorded remark.
Memory hook: Post-dated cheque — payable after the war, if at all.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_15
questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the rejection of the Cripps Mission (1942):
items: 1. The INC objected because it wanted Princely States to be represented in the Constituent Assembly by elected members and not by nominees of the Princes.
2. The Muslim League rejected the offer because it wanted two Constituent Assemblies — one for what would become Pakistan and one for the rest of India.
3. Talks ultimately broke down on the issue of the Viceroy's continued control over Defence during the war.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: (d) ✓ INC objected to nominees of the Princes (citing the 1938 Haripura Session position that Princely States are integral to India); ML1906 wanted two Constituent Assemblies — one for Pakistan and one for the rest of India; and the talks actually broke down on Britain's "take it or leave it" stance on the Viceroy retaining Defence — "no real transfer of executive power."
Why others wrong: (a), (b), (c) each pick only one of three reasons — all three are factually correct.
Memory hook: INC wanted elected Princely reps; ML wanted two CAs; Defence-deadlock killed the deal.

questions.label: FYQ_M.1
questions.stem: WWII fundamentally transformed the Indian National Movement — from a colonial reformist struggle into a movement that could no longer be contained by negotiation. Examine.
body: Demand of the question: "Examine" + "fundamentally transformed" demands tracing the structural shift WWII caused.

Suggested intro (~25 words): Before September 1939, the INM operated within the constitutional reformist framework of GOI 1935. By August 1942 (Quit India), it had broken out of that framework entirely.
Body guidance — 4 themes:

1. The Linlithgow declaration (see '1939: Where Did the INC Stand @WW II?'). Viceroy's unilateral war declaration without consulting elected Indian governments destroyed the legitimacy of the GOI 1935 federal-cooperation framework. The Congress Ministries' resignation (Oct 1939) ended a key British strategy — using elected Indian governments as legitimating instruments.

2. Wardha → August Offer → Individual Satyagraha (see '1939 Wardha Meet of the Congress Working Committee'). Each negotiation revealed the gap: Indians wanted post-war independence commitment + immediate representative government; Britain offered Dominion Status (post-war) + minority veto framework. Cumulative rejection created a constituency for radical action.

3. The Cripps failure (see 'Cripps Mission (1942)'). Sent under pressure (Singapore fall + American pressure on Churchill), Cripps confirmed that no further constitutional advance was possible during the war. Gandhi's "post-dated cheque" phrase captured this. Cripps's failure was the immediate trigger for Quit India.

4. The structural transformation. WWII forced the INM to choose: negotiate within the British framework (which had repeatedly failed) or move outside it. By August 1942, the choice was made — Quit India was the first INM action that explicitly aimed at making British rule administratively unworkable, not at extracting reforms.

Closing verdict: WWII collapsed the negotiation framework. The trajectory Sep-1939 (resignations) → Aug-1940 (Offer rejection) → Oct-1940 (Individual Satyagraha) → Mar-1942 (Cripps failure) → Aug-1942 (Quit India) was a one-way transformation. The pre-war reformist INM could not have produced Quit India; the post-WWII INM could not return to GOI 1935 negotiation.
revise: 1939: Where Did the INC Stand @WW II?

questions.label: FYQ_M.2
questions.stem: Examine the reasons why the Cripps Mission (March 1942) failed despite the British sending their most India-friendly negotiator.
body: Demand of the question: "Examine reasons" + "despite India-friendly" demands explaining why even a sympathetic Cripps couldn't bridge the gap.

Suggested intro (~25 words): Sir Stafford Cripps was a Labour-Left politician with public sympathy for Indian independence. His Mission still failed — because the substance of what Britain could offer fell below what India would accept.
Body guidance — 3 themes (see 'Cripps Mission (1942)'):

1. The Substance Gap. Cripps offered Dominion Status after the war + post-war Constituent Assembly. INC wanted post-war independence + immediate representative government with Indians in the Defence portfolio. The two were structurally incompatible regardless of Cripps's personal goodwill.

2. The Provincial Opt-Out — the Pakistan corridor. The Proposals allowed any province or Princely State to opt out of the Indian Union & form its own dominion. INC saw this as conceding Pakistan by stealth; ML saw it as still inadequate (Pakistan not explicit). Both opposed the same clause for opposite reasons.

3. Cripps's lack of authority. Cripps had no authority to negotiate the offer; his role was to convey Churchill's War Cabinet's pre-decided position. Gandhi's "post-dated cheque on a crashing bank" captured the dual problem — Britain's commitment (post-war) was time-distant, & British military position (Singapore fallen February 1942) was deteriorating.

Closing verdict: Cripps failed because the negotiator was India-friendly but the brief was not. Substance, not personality, drove the failure. The Mission's collapse was the immediate trigger for Quit India (August 1942).

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.1
questions.stem: What is the correct sequence of the following event?
items: 1. the August offer.
2. The I.N.A. trial.
3. The Quit India movement 4. The Royal Indian Naval Ratings Revolt.
questions.stemTail: Select the correct answer using the codes below:
explanation: (C) ✓ — Chronology from the record: the August Offer came in 1940; the Quit India Movement in August 1942; the INA trial in November 1945; and the Naval Ratings Revolt in February 1946. With the stem's numbering, that order reads 1 → 3 → 2 → 4.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Code 1, 2, 3, 4 places the INA trial (November 1945) before the Quit India Movement of 1942 — impossible.
(B) ✗ — Code 3, 1, 2, 4 starts with Quit India (1942) before the August Offer of 1940 — the Offer came first.
(D) ✗ — Code 3, 1, 4, 2 fails twice: Quit India (1942) cannot precede the 1940 August Offer, and the Naval Revolt of February 1946 cannot precede the INA trial of November 1945.
(Note: 1. The August offer 1940
2. Quit India Movement 1942
3. The I.N.A. trial 1945
4. The Royal Indian Naval Revolt 1946)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.2
questions.stem: Assertion [A] Lord Linlithgow described the August Movement of 1942 as the most serious rebellion since Sepoy Mutiny. Reason [R] There was massive upsurge of the peasantry in certain areas. Codes

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: (A) ✓ — Both rich and poor peasants actively participated, and crucially, their anger was directed entirely at the British with no violence against zamindars or moneylenders.
Wrong options:

(B) ✗ — The explanation test fails this option: the massive peasant upsurge — "Peasants were the soul of the QIM(1942-45)" — is precisely why Linlithgow rated it the most serious rebellion since 1857. R does explain A.
(C) ✗ — R is not false: peasants of eastern UP, Bihar, Midnapore and Satara drove the movement, with both rich and poor peasants actively participating.
(D) ✗ — A is not false: Linlithgow's 'most serious rebellion since the Sepoy Mutiny' description is recorded and in the ✓ entry of PYQ_Pre.3.

(Note: The Quit India Movement which was started on 8th August, 1942 had unprecedent involvement of peasant community, which made the struggle more fierce. Thus Lord Linlithgow described this movement as the most serious revolt since 1857.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.3
questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Lord Linlithgow described the August Movement of 1942 as the most serious revolt after the Sepoy Mutiny.
Reason (R): There was a massive upsurge of the peasantry in certain areas.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanaiton of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: (A) ✓ — Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. Linlithgow did make this comparison in correspondence to Churchill; the August 1942 Quit India Movement saw a massive peasant upsurge in Bihar, eastern UP, Bengal and coastal Andhra (parallel governments at Tamluk, Satara, Balia) — making it the most serious revolt since 1857.
Wrong options:
(B) ✗ — R is the explanation: it was the peasant upsurge — parallel governments at Tamluk, Satara and Ballia included — that made the 1942 revolt look like 1857 to Linlithgow.
(C) ✗ — R is not false: the peasantry's massive upsurge is recorded — "Peasants were the soul of the QIM(1942-45)".
(D) ✗ — A is not false: Linlithgow made exactly this comparison in correspondence with Churchill (see the ✓ entry above).

(Note: Due to the involvement of peasants. the Quit India Movement became one of the biggest and most wide spread movement, thus led Linlithgow (1936-44) to call this movement most serious revolt after Sepoy Mutiny of 1857.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.4
questions.stem: Consider the following statements On the eve of launch of Quit India Movement, Mahatma Gandhi
items: 1. asked the government servants to resign.
2. asked the soldiers to leave their posts.
3. asked the princes of the princely states to accept the sovereignty of their own people.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
explanation: (C) ✓ — Per MG's Gowalia Tank speech: government servants were told Do not resign. Stay in your posts but declare your loyalty to the INC; soldiers were told to support the Allied effort "but do not fire on your own countrymen" — not to leave their posts; and the Princes were told to "Accept the sovereignty of your own people". Statements 1 and 2 fail, statement 3 stands — only 3.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Both statements contradict the recorded speech: no resignations were asked of government servants, and soldiers were not asked to desert their posts.
(B) ✗ — Includes statement 2, but soldiers were told to keep supporting the Allied war effort and only refuse to fire on their countrymen.
(D) ✗ — Statements 1 and 2 both fail against MG's recorded instructions to government servants and soldiers — only statement 3 survives.
(Note: Mahatma Gandhi did not ask government servants to resign, but to show their allegiance towards Congress. Soldiers were not asked to leave their post but to not fire on their compaions.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.5
questions.stem: With which one of the following movements is the slogan 'Do or Die' associated?
explanation: (D) ✓ — at the Gowalia Tank meeting on 8 August 1942, MG gave his historic speech — including his famous call 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro). The slogan belongs to the Quit India Movement.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — The Swadeshi Movement (1905–11) belongs to the boycott-Swadeshi era — decades before the Do-or-Die call of 8 August 1942.
(B) ✗ — The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22) was built on withdrawal of cooperation; the Do-or-Die call is dated 8 August 1942.
(C) ✗ — CDM's signature act was the salt satyagraha of 1930; 'Do or Die' came twelve years later, at the QIM launch.

(Note: On 8th August, 1942, the Congress in its meeting at Bombay passed a resolution known as 'Quit India' resolution, whereby Gandhiji asked the British to leave India as soon as possible and gave a call for 'Do or Die'.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.6
questions.stem: During the freedom struggle, Aruna Asaf Ali was a major woman organiser of underground activities in
explanation: (C) ✓ — Aruna Asaf Ali & Sucheta Kriplani were active organisers during the underground phase, and the underground network roster names her again. Her theatre was the Quit India underground.
Wrong options:

(A) ✗ — CDM's recorded women's landmarks carry other names — Sarojini Naidu leading the Dharasana raid, Rukmini Lakshmipathi at Vedaranniyam; Aruna Asaf Ali's recorded organising role is the 1942 underground.
(B) ✗ — The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22) is a generation earlier; no NCM role is recorded for Aruna Asaf Ali — her record is the QIM underground.
(D) ✗ — The Swadeshi Movement ended by 1911 — decades before her underground organising of 1942.

(Note: During the freedom struggle, Aruna Asaf Ali was a major woman organiser of underground activities in Quit India Movement. During Quit India Movement within six or seven months, the repression brought the movement to an end.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.7
questions.stem: With reference to Indian freedom struggle, Usha Mehta is well known for

options.text: running the secret Congress radio in the wake of Quit India Movement
participating in the Second Round Table Conference
leading a contingent of Indian National Army
assisting in the formation of Interim Government under Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru

explanation: (A) ✓ — Usha Mehta ran the Congress Radio to coordinate underground activities — the secret Congress radio of the Quit India underground.
Wrong options:
(B) ✗ — The 2nd RTC (1931) is recorded with Ambedkar and the separate-electorates deadlock; Usha Mehta's recorded contribution is the 1942 underground radio.
(C) ✗ — No INA role is recorded for Usha Mehta — the INA belongs to Bose's campaign abroad; her record is the Congress Radio.
(D) ✗ — The Interim Government belongs to the 1946 endgame after the Cabinet Mission; Usha Mehta's recorded contribution is the underground radio of 1942.

(Note: Usha Mehta was a Gandhian and freedom fighter of India. She is remembered for organising the Congress radio, also called the secret Congress radio, an underground radio station which functioned for few months.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.8
questions.stem: Which one of the following observations is not true about the Quit India Movement of 1942?

options.text: It was led by Mahatma Gandhi
It did not attract the labour class in particular

explanation: (D) ✓ — Statement (d) is the untrue one: labour took part substantially — many worker strikes broke out independently. The Ahmedabad mills saw a strike that lasted 3.5 months — and the labour class agitating through bandhs and hartals.
Wrong options:

(A) ✗ — As conceived it was a Gandhian non-violent call; the violence of the six-week mass phase erupted only after the entire leadership was jailed on 9 August. The untrue observation the examiner wants is (d) — the labour statement.
(B) ✗ — MG did lead it: he drafted the Quit India resolution and gave the Do-or-Die call at Gowalia Tank — a true observation, so not the pick.
(C) ✗ — Its spontaneity is recorded: with the top leadership arrested on the very first night, the movement ran "leaderless at the top" on the public's own understanding — true, so not the pick.
(Note: Indeed a majority of the Quit India Movement was carried by the labour class as they agitated through bandhs and hartals.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.9
questions.stem: Quit India Movement was launched in response to
explanation: (B) ✓ — The failure of the Cripps Mission in 1942 removed the last hope of a negotiated settlement — and After the Cripps Mission collapsed, MG drafted a resolution demanding Quit India.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — The Cabinet Mission came in 1946, four years AFTER the QIM launch — it could not have triggered it.
(C) ✗ — The Simon Commission Report's lineage ran through the RTCs to the GOI Act 1935 — a different chain altogether; QIM's recorded trigger is the Cripps failure.
(D) ✗ — The Wavell Plan belongs to 1945, after the movement had already ended.

(Note: Quit India Movement was launched in August, 1942. It came in response to the Cripps Proposals. The Cripps Mission came to India in March, 1942 and was headed by Sir Stafford Cripps. It had come to negotiate.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.10
questions.stem: With reference to 8th August, 1942 in Indian history, which one of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The Quit India Resolution was adopted by the AICC
The Viceroy's Executive Council was expanded to include more Indians
The Congress ministries resigned in seven provinces
Cripps proposed an Indian Union with full Dominion Status once the Second World War was over

explanation: (A) ✓ — On 8th August 1942, the INC held a special session in Bombay... The QIM(1942-45) Resolution was passed at the session with the demand for immediate Purna Swaraj.
Wrong options:
(B) ✗ — The VEC expansion came in 1941, when Indians rose to 8 of 12 members — not on 8 August 1942.
(C) ✗ — The Congress ministries resigned in 1939 on the Wardha directive — three years before 8 August 1942.
(D) ✗ — Cripps made his Dominion-Status proposal in March 1942 — five months before 8 August, and it was never an event of that date.

(Note: The Quit India Resolution was adopted by the All India Congress Committee (AICC) on 8th August, 1942. In July 1942, the Congress Working Committee met at Wardha and resolved that it would authorize Gandhi.)

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_1
questions.stem: Who coined the slogan "Quit India" later adopted as the name of the 1942 movement?
explanation: Why others wrong: Nehru spoke at Bombay but did not coin the phrase. Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank. Patwardhan led the underground in Satara. Yusuf Meherally — same man who coined "Simon Go Back" — coined "Quit India".
Memory hook: Same pen, two slogans — Simon Go Back, then Quit India.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_2
questions.stem: The phrase "Do or Die" (Karo ya Maro) was given by Mahatma Gandhi at which venue and date?
explanation: Why others wrong: Wardha (July 1942) was the CWC meeting where the idea was accepted, not the public speech. Sabarmati was not the venue. Aga Khan Palace was MG's later place of detention. The public meeting at Gowalia Tank (Azad Maidan) on the evening of 8 August 1942 carried the "Do or Die" call.
Memory hook: Gowalia Tank evening, 8 August — Do or Die.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_3
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the launch of the Quit India Movement:
items: 1. The Quit India Resolution was passed at a special INC session in Bombay on 8 August
2. The Congress Working Committee had accepted the idea at Nagpur in July 1942.
3. The entire top INC leadership was arrested on the night of 9 August 1942.
questions.stemTail: 1942 1942 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: (d) ✓ — (d) ✓ Statements 1 and 3 are exact: the special INC session at Bombay on 8 August 1942 passed the Quit India Resolution, and the entire top INC leadership was arrested that same night of 9 August 1942. Statement 2 moves the venue: the CWC accepted the Quit India idea at Wardha in July 1942 — Nagpur belongs to the 1920 session, where MG began building the INC's grassroots machinery, not to 1942.

Why others wrong: (a) 1 and 2 only — retains statement 2, which puts the July 1942 CWC decision at Nagpur; the CWC accepted the idea at Wardha. (b) 1, 2 and 3 — the tempting all-inclusive option, but it cannot stand once the Wardha/Nagpur swap in statement 2 is spotted. (c) 2 and 3 only — carries the false statement 2 and additionally drops the correct statement 1 (Bombay, 8 August 1942).
Memory hook: Wardha decided in July (not Nagpur — that is 1920), Bombay declared on 8 August, the night of 9 August jailed them all.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_4
questions.stem: Which two major political organisations stayed out of the Quit India Movement?

options.text: Communist Party of India and Muslim League

explanation: Why others wrong: names only two abstainers — the CPI1925 (because the Soviet Union was fighting on the British side) and the ML1906 (which calculated its own gains from the British). Hindu Mahasabha, Forward Bloc, Justice Party, Akali Dal, Liberal Federation and Khudai Khidmatgars are not listed as the two major abstainers.
Memory hook: Two abstainers — Reds following Moscow, League following Jinnah.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_5
questions.stem:
Match the parallel government with its location:
List I (Parallel Govt) — List II (Location)
A. Patri Sarkar —
items:
1. Ballia, Eastern UP
B. Jatiya Sarkar —

2. Satara, Maharashtra
C. First parallel government —
3. Midnapore, Bengal
explanation: Why others wrong: places Patri Sarkar at Satara (Maharashtra), Jatiya Sarkar at Midnapore (Bengal), and the first parallel government at Ballia (Eastern UP, August 1942). Only option (a) maps all three correctly.
Memory hook: Patri-Satara, Jatiya-Midnapore, First-Ballia.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_6
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Patri Sarkar of Satara:
items: 1. It was set up by Nana Patil with guidance from Achyut Patwardhan.
2. It enforced prohibition on alcohol and organised Gandhi Marriages.
3. It functioned continuously from mid-1943 to 1945.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: All three are stated in — Nana Patil set it up with guidance from Achyut Patwardhan (the "Lion of Satara")); it enforced prohibition and organised Gandhi Marriages (where Dalits were invited and given proper respect); it ran continuously from mid-1943 to 1945. Hence all three.
Memory hook: Patri = Patil + Patwardhan + prohibition + 1943-45.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_7
questions.stem: Who led the parallel government at Ballia in August 1942?
explanation: Why others wrong: Nana Patil led the Patri Sarkar at Satara. Y.B. Chavan was a key Satara leader till his arrest at the end of 1942. JP led the Quit India underground. Chittu Pandey led Ballia, overthrew the District Collector, and freed INC leaders from jail.
Memory hook: Ballia's Collector overthrown by Chittu Pandey.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_8
questions.stem: Arrange the following events of the Quit India Movement in correct chronological order:
items: 1. CWC accepts the Quit India idea at Wardha
2. Bombay special session passes the Quit India Resolution
3. Mahadev Desai dies at Aga Khan Palace
4. Kasturba Gandhi dies at Aga Khan Palace
explanation: (a) ✓ — [ The Mass Struggle Phase...) + (The INC Quit India Resolution; The Underground Phase)]

Why others wrong: Wardha (July 1942) came first; Bombay session 8 August 1942; Mahadev Desai died 15 August 1942 at Aga Khan Palace; Kasturba Gandhi died 22 February 1944 at the same palace. Hence the order is 1-2-3-4. Other sequences misplace one or more dates.
Memory hook: Wardha → Bombay → Mahadev (Aug 1942) → Kasturba (Feb 1944).

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_9
questions.stem: Which legal instruments did the British use for preventive detention and crackdown during the Quit India Movement?

options.text: Revolutionary Movement Ordinance and Defence of India Rules
Vernacular Press Act and Arms Act
Government of India Act 1935 and Indian Penal Code

explanation: Why others wrong: specifically names the Revolutionary Movement Ordinance and the Defence of India Rules (which gave powers of preventive detention). Rowlatt, Vernacular Press, Arms Act and the GoI Act 1935 are not the QIM-era crackdown instruments.
Memory hook: Two tools of 1942 — RMO + DIR.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_10
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the underground phase of the Quit India Movement:
items: 1. The Congress Socialist Party provided most of its leadership.
2. Usha Mehta ran the Congress Radio to coordinate underground activities.
3. Sumati Morarjee gave Jayaprakash Narayan a different car every single day.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: (a) ✓ — [ + ] Statements 1 and 2 hold: the underground leadership came primarily from the Congress Socialist Party, and Usha Mehta ran the Congress Radio to coordinate underground activities. Statement 3 changes the recipient: Sumati Morarjee's daily change of car was given to Achyut Patwardhan so he could not be tracked, not to Jayaprakash Narayan — both men led the same underground network, which is precisely why the two get mixed up.

Why others wrong: (b) 1 and 3 only — keeps the false statement 3 (the cars went to Achyut Patwardhan, not JP) and drops the correct Usha Mehta statement. (c) 2 and 3 only — same false statement 3, and it also discards the correct attribution of the underground leadership to the Congress Socialist Party. (d) 1, 2 and 3 — the all-inclusive option fails on statement 3 alone; statements 1 and 2 are correct, so (a) is the only complete-and-true set.
Memory hook: CSP brains, Usha's radio, Sumati's daily car — and that car was Patwardhan's, not JP's.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_11
questions.stem: Who was given the title "Lion of Satara" for his role in guiding the Patri Sarkar?
explanation: Why others wrong: Nana Patil set up the Patri Sarkar but was not titled "Lion of Satara". Y.B. Chavan was the most important leader until his arrest at the end of 1942 but did not hold this title. JP led the underground nationally. specifically gives the title "Lion of Satara" to Achyut Patwardhan.
Memory hook: Patwardhan = Lion of Satara.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_12
questions.stem: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
items: 1. Cripps Mission fails
2. Bombay session passes Quit India Resolution
3. Mahatma Gandhi begins his 21-day fast at Aga Khan Palace
4. Mahatma Gandhi is released from detention
explanation: (a) ✓ — [ + The Mass Struggle Phase...) + (The Underground Phase) + (Reasons; Resolution; Underground Phase; How QIM Ended)]

Why others wrong: Cripps failed in 1942 before the Bombay session of 8 August 1942). MG's 21-day fast came during his detention at Aga Khan Palace (1943). His release on health grounds came in May 1944. Hence 1-2-3-4.
Memory hook: Cripps → Bombay → Fast (1943) → Release (May 1944).

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_13
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about results of the Quit India Movement ('Results and Significance of the QIM(1942-45)'):
items: 1. It was the first movement to make the world take notice of India's demand for freedom.
2. The loyalty of the British administrative machinery broke.
3. Parallel governments showed Indians could self-govern.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
