explanation: (b) ✓ — (b) ✓ Statements 2 and 3 are listed results: the loyalty of the British administrative machinery broke (officials leaking raid plans, police looking away, Indian members of the Viceroy's Executive Council resigning), and the parallel governments — Ballia, the Jatiya Sarkar, the Patri Sarkar — showed Indians could self-govern. Statement 1 belongs to the earlier movement: the chapter's own verdict is that the CDM (1930–34) made the world notice India's demand, while the QIM made the world accept that the demand could not be denied.

Why others wrong: (a) 1 and 2 only — retains statement 1; first world notice is credited to the CDM (1930–34), not to the QIM. (c) 1 and 3 only — same false statement 1, and it also drops the correct statement 2 on the collapse of administrative loyalty. (d) 1, 2 and 3 — the all-inclusive option looks safe because statements 2 and 3 are textbook results, but statement 1 shifts a CDM result onto the QIM.
Memory hook: CDM made the world notice; QIM made the world accept — broken steel frame + parallel governments are the QIM's own results.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_14
questions.stem:
Match the personality with their Quit India role:
List I (Personality) — List II (Role)
A. Aruna Asaf Ali —
items:
1. Ran the Congress Radio underground
B. Usha Mehta —

2. Hoisted the national flag at Gowalia Tank
C. Mirabehn —
3. Gandhi's English disciple, imprisoned with Gandhi
matchTable: Hoisted the national flag at Gowalia Tank
Gandhi's English disciple, imprisoned with Gandhi
explanation: Why others wrong: places Aruna Asaf Ali and Sucheta Kriplani as underground organisers, with Aruna Asaf Ali noted as the flag-hoister at Gowalia Tank. names Usha Mehta as the Congress Radio operator. describes Mirabehn (Madeleine Slade) as Gandhi's English disciple, imprisoned alongside him. Only (a) maps all three.
Memory hook: Aruna-flag, Usha-radio, Mira-disciple.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_15
questions.stem: When and through which event did the Quit India Movement formally end?

options.text: Gandhi's release from Aga Khan Palace in May 1944
End of World War II and the Simla Conference of June 1945

explanation: Why others wrong: Gandhi's May 1944 release was on health grounds — the movement did not end then; he turned to constructive work. The Cabinet Mission (1946) and Mountbatten Plan (1947) came later. states the QIM formally ended when all INC leaders were released in June 1945 to participate in the Simla Conference.
Memory hook: War ends, Simla begins, QIM closes — June 1945.

questions.label: FYQ_M.1
questions.stem: The Quit India Movement (1942-45) was the most radical departure of the INM from constitutional politics. Examine its causes, course & long-term significance.
body: Demand of the question: "Examine" + "causes/course/long-term" = comprehensive treatment.
Suggested intro (~25 words): QIM was not just another mass movement — it was the INM's first declaration that British rule was illegitimate by definition, not merely reformable.
Body guidance — 4 themes:

1. Causes (see 'Reasons for Launching the QIM(1942-45)'). Cumulative failure of negotiation: Linlithgow 1939 + August Offer 1940 + Cripps 1942. War-time British weakness: Singapore fall, Burma loss, Japanese threat. Inflation, food shortage, repression. Time pressure: Japanese advance meant Britain might collapse before INC could act.

2. Course (see 'Events During the QIM(1942-45) (1942)'). Bombay AICC resolution 8 Aug 1942 + Gandhi's "Do or Die" + Operation Zero Hour mass arrests + underground leadership (Jayaprakash Narayan, Lohia, Aruna Asaf Ali, Usha Mehta) + Parallel Governments (Tamluk, Satara, Ballia, Talcher) + railway/telegraph sabotage. Largely leaderless, locally improvised within broad QIM framework.

3. British Response (see 'Events During the QIM(1942-45) (1942)'). Brutal repression: ~10,000 killed, ~60,000+ arrested, public floggings, machine-gunning of crowds. The movement was crushed militarily by mid-1943 but never declared formally suspended.

4. Long-term Significance (see 'Results and Significance of the QIM(1942-45)'). Established INC's mass legitimacy as the only viable INM voice. Demonstrated administrative ungovernability — Britain could not rule a hostile India indefinitely. Forced post-war Labour government to accelerate transfer-of-power negotiations (Cabinet Mission 1946). Provided ideological context for INA's parallel armed struggle.

Closing verdict: QIM did not "win" in the immediate sense — it was crushed. But it changed the British calculation. By 1945, the question was no longer "should we transfer power" but "to whom & on what terms". The strategic victory was structural — Britain accepted that continued rule was untenable, even before Japan was defeated.

questions.label: FYQ_M.2
questions.stem: The Parallel Governments formed during the Quit India Movement (1942-44) are a unique feature of Indian nationalism. Examine their character & limits.
body: Demand of the question: "Examine character & limits" demands both halves.

Suggested intro (~25 words): During QIM, four major Parallel Governments operated — Tamluk (Bengal), Satara (Maharashtra), Ballia (UP), Talcher (Odisha) — each a local non-British administration claiming legitimate authority.
Body guidance — 3 themes (see 'Events During the QIM(1942-45) (1942)'):

1. Their Character. Local citizens organized their own taxation, justice, education, & welfare systems in defiance of British administration. Tamralipta Sarkar (Tamluk, Midnapore) lasted ~21 months — collected revenue, ran schools, judicial panchayats. Satara's "Prati Sarkar" under Y.B. Chavan + Nana Patil operated similarly.

2. Their Significance. Demonstrated the practical possibility of post-British self-government at the local level. Provided training in administrative self-rule for nationalist cadres. Showed the British that authority could be locally substituted, not just symbolically protested.

3. Their Limits. Geographically restricted to specific districts; could not function in cities (Bombay, Calcutta). Required British military weakness — once the British returned with reinforcement, each Parallel Government was crushed within weeks. They were episodic, not sustained alternatives to British rule.

Closing verdict: Parallel Governments were laboratory experiments in self-rule — proving administrative feasibility but unable to sustain against full British military repression. Their legacy lies in cadre experience, not in territorial achievement.

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.1
questions.stem: The Indian National Army (INA) came into existence in 1943 in
explanation: (C) ✓ — Singapore: Following the fall of Singapore in February 1942, Captain Mohan Singh conceived the idea of the INA by organising Indian PoWs... 40,000 PoWs in Singapore joined — and it was at Singapore in July 1943 that Netaji took over the INA and went on to proclaim the Provisional Government. (See the ⚠ Prelims Trap in on the 1942-vs-1943 date.)
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Japan was the patron power and the place of R.B. Bose's exile, but the army itself was raised at Singapore from the Indian PoWs handed over there.
(B) ✗ — Rangoon (Burma) became an INA headquarters only after the Provisional Government was set up in October 1943; the force originated at Singapore.
(D) ✗ — Malaya was the first of the three territories Japan overran in early 1942 — context, not birthplace: the PoW regrouping that created the INA happened at Singapore.
(Note: INA was an armed force formed by Indian nationalists in 1942 in South-East Asia during World War II. The aim of the army was to secure Indian Independence with Japanese assistance.
Initially formed in 1942 under Captain Mohan Singh, it was later revived in 1943 under Subhas Chandra Bose.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.3
questions.stem: Which one of the following suggested the reconstitution of the Viceroy's Executive Council in which all the portfolios including that of war members were to be held by the Indian leaders?
explanation: (B) ✓ — The Wavell Plan, placed before the Simla Conference of June 1945, proposed reconstituting the Viceroy's Executive Council with all portfolios — including the War Member's — in Indian hands. All INC leaders were released in June 1945 precisely to attend this conference.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — The Simon Commission's recorded recommendations were provincial autonomy with "No change at the Centre" — the opposite of Indianising the Viceroy's Executive Council.
(C) ✗ — Cripps offered no such Indianisation: Defence stayed with the Viceroy and there was to be "no dilution of the Viceroy's powers over ministers" — the talks broke down on exactly that point.
(D) ✗ — The Cabinet Mission came later, in 1946, to settle the constitution-making question — not to reconstitute the wartime Executive Council.
(Note: The plan suggested the reconstitution of the Viceroy's Executive Council. Different Communities were to get their due share in the council and parity was reserved for cast Hindus and Muslims.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.4
questions.stem: During the Indian Freedom Struggle, who of the following raised an army called 'Free Indian Legion'?
explanation: (C) ✓ — During the Indian freedom struggle, the free Indian Legion was established by Subhash Chandra Bose. In Singapore, in 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose formed the Azad Hind Faui (Indian National Army) and gave his famous call 'Delhi Chalo'. Rash Behari Bose, who had been living in exile in Japan since 1915 joined him. Subhash Chandra Bose popularly known as 'Netaji' was born on 23rd January, 1897, at Cutt
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Lala Hardayal's theatre was the Ghadar Movement of 1913–15 — a generation before the Free Indian Legion, which Bose raised in Germany (see the ✓ entry above).
(B) ✗ — Rash Behari Bose's recorded INA role was caretaker leadership in early 1943, handed over to Netaji at Singapore; the Free Indian Legion of Germany was Netaji's creation (✓ entry above).
(D) ✗ — No army-raising is recorded for Savarkar in these chapters; the Free Indian Legion belongs to Netaji's Germany phase — the same phase as his Azad Hind Radio broadcasts.

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.5
questions.stem: With reference to Indian freedom struggle, consider the following events :
items: 1. Mutiny in Royal Indian Navy
2. Quit India Movement launched
3. Second Round Table Conference
questions.stemTail: What is the correct chronological sequence of the above events ?
explanation: (C) ✓ — Chronology from the record: the 2nd Round Table Conference sat September–December 1931; the Quit India Movement was launched in August 1942; the Naval Ratings Mutiny came in February 1946. Order: 3 – 2 – 1.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Code 1-2-3 reverses the line completely: it puts the 1946 mutiny first and the 1931 RTC last.
(B) ✗ — Code 2-1-3 starts with Quit India (1942) and ends with the 2nd RTC — but the RTC (1931) came first of the three.
(D) ✗ — Code 3-1-2 places the Naval Mutiny (February 1946) before Quit India (August 1942) — impossible.
(Note: Mutiny of Royal Indian Navy broke in February, 1946 at Bombay on Talwar ship and in Karachi at Hindustan ship. Quit India Movement is launched on 9th August, 1942 at Bombay.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.6
questions.stem: In the context of Colonial India, Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sehgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon are remembered as

options.text: leaders of Swadeshi and Boycott Movement
members of the Interim Government in 1946
members of the Drafting Committee in the Constituent Assembly
officers of the Indian National Army

explanation: (D) ✓ — The most famous trial was held at the Red Fort: Shah Nawaz Khan (a close aide of Netaji), Prem Sehgal, and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon were the accused. They are remembered as officers of the INA.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — The Swadeshi and Boycott Movement belongs to 1905–11 — a different generation; the trio's record is the Red Fort INA trial of November 1945.
(B) ✗ — The Interim Government of 1946 carries a different cast; in 1945–46 these three men were standing trial at the Red Fort.

(C) ✗ — The Drafting Committee belongs to the Constituent Assembly's constitution-writing work; the recorded fame of Khan, Sehgal and Dhillon is as the three INA accused — Muslim, Hindu and Sikh — whose trial united the country.

(Note: Major General Shah Nawaz Khan, Colonel Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon and Colonel Prem Kumar Sehgal were the officers of the Indian National Army (INA). They were captured by the British when INA was defeated.)

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_1
questions.stem: Who first conceived and organised the Indian National Army (INA) by mobilising Indian Prisoners of War after the fall of Singapore in February 1942?
explanation: Why others wrong: (a) Subhas Bose took over INA leadership only in July 1943, not 1942. (b) Rash Behari Bose took over leadership in early 1943, after Mohan Singh's arrest. (d) Pritam Singh helped set up the Indian Independence League (IIL) in Bangkok in June 1942, not the INA's First Division.
Memory hook: Mohan Singh = INA's first spark; Bose lit the flame later.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_2
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Bengal Famine of 1943:
items: 1. It was caused primarily by a failure of crops in Bengal.
2. Food supplies from India were diverted to Europe to feed British soldiers and European civilians.
3. The Japanese occupation of Burma stopped food imports that Bengal had been receiving.
4. Viceroy Linlithgow's request for food and a ban on food exports was denied by Prime Minister Churchill.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 1 is incorrect — the record explicitly states it was a man-made famine, not a crop failure; roughly 5 million Indians died. Statements 2, 3 and 4 are directly supported by the record. Options (a), (c) and (d) all incorrectly include statement 1.
Memory hook: Not crops failing — entitlements falling.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_3
questions.stem: With reference to Subhas Chandra Bose's journey from India to South-East Asia (1941–1943), arrange the following events in correct chronological order:
items: 1. Arrival in Germany
2. Escape from house arrest in Calcutta in disguise as an Afghan
3. Setting up of Azad Hind Radio
4. Arrival in Singapore and taking over INA leadership
explanation: Why others wrong: Bose escaped Calcutta in January 1941 (after release from a hunger strike), reached Germany in March 1941, set up Azad Hind Radio in 1942 from Germany, and reached Singapore in July 1943 — giving the order 2 → 1 → 3 → 4. (b) and (d) place Germany arrival before the Calcutta escape. (c) places Azad Hind Radio before reaching Germany.
Memory hook: Escape, Berlin, Radio, Rangoon — the four stations of Netaji's odyssey.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_4
questions.stem:
Match List I (Regiment / Unit of the INA) with List II (Distinctive feature) and select the correct answer:
| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| A. Rani Jhansi Regiment |
items:
1. All-women NRI regiment |
| B. First Division |

2. Formally established in September 1942 |
| C. Provisional Government of Free India |

3. Established on 21st October 1943 |
| D. INA marching song |
4. Qadam Qadam Badhaye Ja |
matchTable: List I (List I (Regiment / Unit of the INA))
explanation: Why others wrong: the Rani Jhansi Regiment was the all-women NRI regiment (A-1); the INA's First Division was formally established in September 1942 (B-2); the Provisional Government of Free India was established on 21st October 1943 (C-3); the INA marching song was Qadam Qadam Badhaye Ja (D-4). (a), (b) and (c) all break at least one of these established pairings.
Memory hook: Rani, First, Provisional, Qadam — one for each pillar of Azad Hind.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_5
questions.stem: Where did Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose establish the Provisional Government of Free India on 21st October 1943?
explanation: Why others wrong: (a) Tokyo was not the headquarters of the Provisional Government; Japan only provided assurance of non-annexation via General Tojo. (c) Berlin was where Bose set up Azad Hind Radio in 1942 — not the Provisional Government. (d) Port Blair was visited by Bose on 29–31 December 1943 to hoist the flag and rename the islands; the Provisional Government's headquarters were not there.
Memory hook: INA HQ — Rangoon for Burma, Singapore for South-East Asia.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_6
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the INA Trials at the Red Fort (November 1945):
items: 1. The three accused — Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Sehgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon — represented three religious communities.
2. The defence panel included Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Jawaharlal Nehru and Asaf Ali.
3. Government officials openly supported the movement and contributed money for INA men.
4. The trials were the first instance in Indian history where the INC chose not to be involved in the legal defence.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 4 is incorrect — the INC actively fought cases for the accused under Bhulabhai Desai and set up an INA Relief Committee; it did not stay away. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all explicitly supported by the record. Options (a), (b) and (d) misjudge at least one statement.
Memory hook: Red Fort — three faiths in the dock, the whole nation in the gallery.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_7
questions.stem: Who, in 1943, took over the leadership of the Indian National Army before handing it over to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose in Singapore in July 1943?
explanation: Why others wrong: (a) Captain Mohan Singh, the INA's founder, was arrested by the Japanese in December 1942 and was not the intermediate leader in 1943. (c) Pritam Singh helped set up the Indian Independence League in Bangkok in June 1942, not the INA. (d) Shah Nawaz Khan was a close aide of Netaji and an accused in the Red Fort INA Trials, not a leader of the INA in early 1943.
Memory hook: Mohan → R.B. Bose → Netaji — three batons, one army.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_8
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Naval Ratings Mutiny of February 1946:
items: 1. It began on His Majesty's Indian Ship (HMIS) Talwar.
2. The ratings hoisted the tricolour alongside flags of the INA, the INC and the Muslim League.
3. Mahatma Gandhi and the INC openly led the ratings to a final victory.
4. Aruna Asaf Ali provided leadership to the ratings despite opposition from Gandhi and the INC.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 3 is incorrect — Gandhi and the INC felt it was a truce period and time for negotiations; they did NOT lead the ratings to victory, and the INC's withdrawal of support helped end the mutiny. Statements 1, 2 and 4 are all directly supported by the record. Options (a), (b) and (c) mis-include statement 3.
Memory hook: Talwar, tricolour, Aruna — the rating's revolt that the Mahatma would not bless.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_9
questions.stem: With reference to the Bengal Famine of 1943 and its aftermath, which one of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Amartya Sen's "entitlement failure" theory explained the famine as a failure of access rather than of supply.
The Famine Inquiry Commission of 1945, headed by Sir John Woodhead, held the colonial administration fully accountable.
Viceroy Linlithgow refused to forward any request to London for food relief.
Public opinion in Britain remained largely unaffected by the famine.

explanation: Why others wrong: (b) The Woodhead Commission largely blamed natural factors and was criticised for NOT holding the colonial administration adequately accountable. (c) Viceroy Linlithgow did request food and proposed a ban on food exports from Bengal — it was Churchill who denied both. (d) British public opinion shifted noticeably; by 1943 most British politicians were sympathetic to Indian independence.
Memory hook: Amartya Sen — famine is empty pockets, not empty fields.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_10
questions.stem: Arrange the following events related to the Indian National Army and the Naval Mutiny in correct chronological order:
items: 1. Formal establishment of the INA's First Division
2. Establishment of the Provisional Government of Free India
3. Beginning of the INA Trials at the Red Fort
4. Outbreak of the Naval Ratings Mutiny on HMIS Talwar
explanation: Why others wrong: Dates: First Division — September 1942; Provisional Government — 21st October 1943; INA Trials — November 1945; Naval Ratings Mutiny — February 1946. Correct order is 1 → 2 → 3 → 4, which is (a). (b), (c) and (d) all break this sequence at least once.
Memory hook: 1942 Division, 1943 Government, 1945 Trial, 1946 Mutiny.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_11
questions.stem:
Match List I (Person) with List II (Role in events of 1942–1946) and select the correct answer:
| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| A. Bhulabhai Desai |
items:
1. Lead lawyer for INA accused at the Red Fort trials |
| B. Aruna Asaf Ali |

2. Provided leadership to naval ratings in Bombay |
| C. Sir John Woodhead |

3. Headed the Famine Inquiry Commission (1945) |
| D. Rama Krishna |
4. Set up the Indian Independence League branch in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands |
matchTable: List II (List II (Role in events of 1942–1946))
Lead lawyer for INA accused at the Red Fort trials
Provided leadership to naval ratings in Bombay
Set up the Indian Independence League branch in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands
explanation: Why others wrong: Bhulabhai Desai (INC leader) fought cases for the INA accused — A-1; Aruna Asaf Ali advised the naval ratings despite Gandhi & INC opposition — B-2; Sir John Woodhead headed the Famine Inquiry Commission (1945) — C-3; Rama Krishna set up the IIL branch in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands in April 1942 — D-4. Options (b), (c) and (d) each break at least one verified pairing.
Memory hook: Desai-Court, Aruna-Bombay, Woodhead-Famine, Krishna-Andamans.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_12
questions.stem: Which one of the following slogans was NOT given to India by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose?

options.text: Qadam Qadam Badhaye Ja (as INA marching song)

explanation: Why others wrong: Netaji gave India the slogans Jai Hind and Delhi Chalo, and Qadam Qadam Badhaye Ja was the INA marching song — so (a), (b) and (d) are all attributable to Bose / the INA. (c) "Karo Ya Maro" is not associated with Bose; it belongs to a different stream of the freedom struggle and is the answer to "NOT".
Memory hook: Jai Hind, Delhi Chalo, Qadam Qadam — Bose's three INA war-cries.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_13
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Kohima & Imphal Campaign of 1944:
items: 1. The campaign was a joint INA–Japanese attack on the India–Burma border.
2. The campaign ended in success for the INA, leading to the liberation of Imphal.
3. Indian INA soldiers were discriminated against by the Japanese in the allocation of weapons and supplies.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 2 is incorrect — the record states the campaign "failed". Statements 1 and 3 are directly supported by the record. Hence only (d) — "1 and 3 only" — is correct; (a) is incomplete, and (b) & (c) wrongly include statement 2.
Memory hook: Imphal failed — and even the ally short-changed the soldier.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_14
questions.stem: With reference to the impact of the Naval Ratings Mutiny and the Royal Indian Air Force (RIAF) strikes of 1946, which one of the following statements is correct?

options.text: They strengthened the British belief that the "martial races" of India would always remain loyal to the Crown.
They demonstrated that the British had irrevocably lost control of the Indian armed forces.
After independence, almost all participating naval ratings were recruited into the Indian armed forces.
The mutiny was suppressed entirely by British repression, without any role for the INC or the Muslim League.

explanation: Why others wrong: (a) The mutinies SHATTERED the "martial races" myth — the opposite of strengthening it. (c) After independence, most INA men & naval ratings were NOT recruited into the armed forces, on grounds of breach of discipline. (d) British repression played a role, but so did the withdrawal of support by the INC & the Muslim League — Sardar Patel and Jinnah personally held meetings to calm the ratings down.
Memory hook: When the Navy raised the tricolour, the "martial races" myth sank.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_15
questions.stem: Where did Captain Mohan Singh first organise the Indian National Army by mobilising Indian Prisoners of War in 1942?
explanation: Why others wrong: (a) Bangkok was the location where the Indian Independence League (IIL) was set up in June 1942 — not the INA. (b) Rangoon (Burma) later became one of the headquarters of the Provisional Government of Free India in October 1943 — not where Mohan Singh first organised the INA. (c) Tokyo was where Rash Behari Bose had escaped to after the Ghadar Movement; the INA was not first organised there.
Memory hook: Singapore falls (Feb 1942) — and the INA rises from its PoW camps.

questions.label: FYQ_M.1
questions.stem: The Indian National Army (1942-45) was militarily defeated but politically transformative. Examine.
body: Demand of the question: "Examine" + "defeated but transformative" demands distinguishing military outcome from political consequence.

Suggested intro (~25 words): INA never captured an Indian city; its forces retreated from Imphal-Kohima by August 1944; Bose died in August 1945. Yet INA's political effect was disproportionate to its military record.
Body guidance — 4 themes:

1. The military record (see 'Indian National Army / Azad Hind Fauj (1942–1945)'). INA reached Imphal & Kohima in March-April 1944 with Japanese support but couldn't sustain — British counter-offensive + monsoon + supply collapse forced retreat. By August 1944, INA was in administrative retreat; Japan's defeat in August 1945 ended INA's external base.

2. The Trials transformed perception (see 'INA Trials and INA Agitations (November 1945 – 1946)'). Red Fort Trials Nov 1945 made INA the focal point of post-war nationalism. The three defendants (Hindu/Muslim/Sikh) symbolised inter-community unity; their defence panel (Bhulabhai Desai + Nehru + Sapru + Asaf Ali) made the trials INC's political theatre. Public agitation forced sentence remission — establishing INA cadres as nationalist heroes, not traitors.

3. The military demonstration effect (see 'The Naval Ratings Mutiny (February 1946)'). RIN Mutiny February 1946 — sailors explicitly invoked INA inspiration. The Mutiny showed the British that even loyalist military forces could not be trusted indefinitely. This is the most direct evidence of INA's transformative effect on Indian military thinking.

4. The political accelerant. INA + Trials + RIN Mutiny convinced post-war Labour government that holding India militarily was unsustainable. Cabinet Mission 1946, Mountbatten 1947, & rapid transfer-of-power followed. Without the INA's political legacy, the timetable would have been different.

Closing verdict: INA's military legacy is small. Its political legacy — disrupting the British loyalist-military framework, accelerating transfer-of-power decisions, providing the symbolic anchor of post-1945 nationalism — is large. The legitimacy of the INA's struggle was vindicated by India's 1972 official recognition as "Freedom Fighters".
revise: INA founding + Azad Hind Government + Imphal-Kohima

questions.label: FYQ_M.2
questions.stem: The Bengal Famine of 1943 was not a natural disaster but an administrative & policy failure. Examine.
body: Demand of the question: "Examine" + "not natural but administrative" demands tracing causes beyond food production failure.

Suggested intro (~25 words): Death toll 2-3 million. Bengal had near-normal rice production in 1942-43. The famine was not caused by absolute food shortage — but by entitlement collapse, hoarding & British policy.
Body guidance — 3 themes (see 'Bengal Famine (1943)'):

1. Entitlement Collapse. Amartya Sen's analysis: rural workers, fisherfolk, artisans lost income because wartime urban inflation diverted purchasing power. Their entitlement to food collapsed even though absolute food availability did not. The poor starved not because food was absent but because they couldn't buy it.

2. British "Denial Policy". Japanese threat from Burma prompted British "denial policy" in coastal Bengal — destruction of boats (denying transport to a potential Japanese invasion), removal of rice stocks from coastal areas. The boats were used by Bengali fisherfolk; their livelihoods collapsed.

3. War-time Procurement & Churchill's Hand. British military procured rice for Indian army + war supplies. Churchill diverted food shipments away from Bengal even when Australia & Canada offered food aid. Press censorship hid the famine; Calcutta's commercial elite hoarded rice for speculation. Administrative response was slow & inadequate.

Closing verdict: Bengal 1943 was a policy famine — produced by war-time British administrative decisions, racial indifference (Churchill's "Indians breed like rabbits" remark), & speculative hoarding. Natural causes were marginal; political causes were primary.

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.1
questions.stem: Which one of the following is not correct about the Cabinet Mission Plan?
explanation: (C) ✓ — Statement (c) is the non-feature: CMP1946 was the only proposal where the British offered a united India & Purna Swaraj — it turned down the demand for a separate Pakistan. At most it carried implicit grouping, never acceptance of Pakistan.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Provincial grouping was a real CMP feature — provinces were divided into Sections A, B and C, each framing a group constitution — so it cannot be the 'not correct' pick.

(B) ✗ — An Interim Cabinet of Indians was also a real feature: Immediate transfer of executive power to an interim government at the Centre. (This was done in September 1946, with J.L. Nehru as Prime Minister.).

(D) ✗ — The constitution-framing right was central to the plan: a Constituent Assembly of elected PLA members plus Princely-State nominees was to frame the constitution — a real feature, not the answer.
(Note: The Cabinet mission plan recommended an undivided India. It turned down the Muslim League's demand for a separate Pakistan.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.2
questions.stem: Assertion (A) The British sovereignty continued to exist in free India. Reason (R) The British sovereign appointed the last Governor General of Free India. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct?

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

explanation: (D) ✓ — A is false, R is true. Free India was sovereign: Yes, symbolic sovereignty continued to exist for crown and dominion status itself lasted only until 26 January 1950 but in the strict language of constitutional law (and UPSC answer keys), "symbolic sovereignty of the Crown" is not the same as "British sovereignty" which implies actual powers to rule India. Indian Independence Act 1947 explicitly ended the British Parliament of any power to legislate for India from the appointed day (15th Aug 1947). R is true: Each dominion would be headed by a Governor General appointed by the King — Mountbatten.
Wrong options:

(A) ✗ — Treats A as true, but British sovereignty did not continue: the Act ended the British Parliament's jurisdiction on the appointed day — the Crown's residual dominion link was terminable, and terminated, by India's own Constituent Assembly.
(B) ✗ — Also treats A as true; it fails the same way — sovereignty had passed: jurisdiction of the British Parliament ended and Paramountcy lapsed on the appointed day.
(C) ✗ — R is not false: the Governor General of each dominion was "appointed by the King" — the British sovereign did appoint free India's last Governor General.
(Note: India became sovereign nation on 15 August, 1947. However Lord Mountabatten as a last Governor General of free India was appointed by British sovereign.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.3
questions.stem: Who among the following suggested the winding up of the Indian National Congress after India attained independence?
explanation: (C) ✓ — Mahatma Gandhi: he asked the top Congress leaders to dissolve the party after freedom and build a new organisation to serve the people — in his view INC's task, the fight for freedom, ended with independence.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Rajagopalachari's recorded instrument was the 1944 formula for an INC-ML settlement; no party-dissolution call is recorded for him — that suggestion was Gandhi's.
(B) ✗ — Kripalani was the INC President of 1947 — he was heading the party, not proposing to wind it up.
(D) ✗ — Jayaprakash Narayan's recorded platform is the Congress Socialist Party; the dissolution suggestion is recorded as Gandhi's.

(Note: Gandhiji had asked all the top Congress leaders to dissolve the party and from a new organisation to serve the people. He told them that the task of INC was to fight for the freedom and liberation of India.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.4
questions.stem: B.R. Ambedkar was elected to the Constituent Assembly from
explanation: (A) ✓ — West Bengal: though Ambedkar resided in the Bombay Presidency, he was not elected from there — his Constituent Assembly seat came from West Bengal. (The CA itself was elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies)
Wrong options:
(B) ✗ — The trap option: Bombay Presidency was Ambedkar's place of residence, but he was not elected from there — his seat was West Bengal.
(C) ✗ — No Madhya Bharat election is recorded for Ambedkar; the recorded seat is West Bengal.
(D) ✗ — Punjab returned no Ambedkar seat; the recorded election is from West Bengal.
(Note: Though he was a resident of Bombay Presidency. He was not elected from there and elected from West Bengal.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.5
questions.stem: At the time India's Independence, Mahatma Gandhi was

options.text: a member of Congress working committee
not a member of the Congress
the General Secretary of the Congress

explanation: (B) ✓ — at independence Mahatma Gandhi was not a member of Congress though he was a mentor — the 1947 party President was J.B. Kripalani. By mid-1947 Gandhi stood outside and alone, Mountbatten's "one-man boundary force" against communal violence.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — He sat on no Working Committee in 1947 — the record is that he was not a Congress member at all.
(C) ✗ — The Congress President of 1947 was J.B. Kripalani, not Gandhi — who held no party office.
(D) ✗ — No General-Secretaryship is recorded; Gandhi stood outside the formal organisation as its moral mentor.
(Note: The president of the Indian National Congress during 1947 was J.B. Kriplani. Mahatma Gandhi was not a member of Congress though he was a mentor for national policy formation.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.6
questions.stem: When the Indian Muslim League was included into the interim government in 1946, Liyaqat Ali Khan was assigned the portfolio of
explanation: (C) ✓ — ML1906 got the Finance Ministry & used it to ensure the government could not function. Liaqat Ali Khan held Finance — Nehru Foreign Affairs, Patel Home, Baldev Singh Defence.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Foreign Affairs was Nehru's portfolio in the Interim Government; the League's prize was Finance.
(B) ✗ — Home was Sardar Patel's; Liaqat Ali Khan sat on Finance, from where ML1906 could throttle the government.
(D) ✗ — Defence went to Baldev Singh; Liaqat's Finance portfolio was chosen precisely for its power to obstruct.
(Note: Foreign Affairs- Jawaharlal Nehru Home - Vallabhabhai Patel Finance - Liyaqat Ali Khan Defence - Baldev Singh)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.7
questions.stem: Lord Mountbatten came to India as Viceroy along with specific instruction to

options.text: persuade the Congress to accept partition

explanation: (B) ✓ — Mountbatten came with a specific instruction to keep India united if possible, with transfer of power no later than 30 June 1948. The record matches: he was given a deadline of October 1947 to explore options for unity & partition.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Reversed: 'Plan Balkan' was Mountbatten's own April 1947 proposal, killed by Nehru's opposition — it was not the instruction he carried from London, which put unity first.
(C) ✗ — His brief was to try unity first; only after two months in India did he conclude that the Cabinet Mission Plan and a united India were "dead horses — entirely due to Jinnah".
(D) ✗ — Persuading Congress toward partition was the eventual outcome, not the instruction: the recorded brief was to keep India united if possible.
(Note: He came with a specific instruction to keep India united if possible, and overseeing the transition of British India to Independence no later than 30th June, 1948.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.8
questions.stem: The Indian National Congress agreed in 1947 to the partition of the country mainly because

options.text: The principle of two Nation theory was then acceptable to them
It was imposed by the British Government and the Congress was helpless in this regard
They wanted to avoid large scale communal riots
India would have otherwise lost the opportunity to attain freedom

explanation: (C) ✓ — By June 1947, INC had given up on a united India — defeated by a combination of communal violence, the failure of the Interim Government, and ML1906's refusal to join the Constituent Assembly. Direct Action Day alone had killed 5,000 in Calcutta in one week. Avoiding ever-larger communal slaughter was the operative reason.
Wrong options:

(A) ✗ — INC never accepted the Two-Nation theory: even its Cabinet-Mission objection was only to compulsory grouping, not to a united India, and Gandhi told INC — "don't accept partition in your hearts" (11.4(v)).
(B) ✗ — Not helpless imposition: INC accepted the 3rd June Plan with its own counter-demands met — Pakistan as small as possible, a strong unitary centre for India.
(D) ✗ — Freedom was already coming: the Atlee Statement had fixed a British exit by 30 June 1948 "with or without a constitution". The recorded driver of acceptance was the communal violence.

(Note: The period of 1940s were the considered crisis time for Hindu Muslim unity thereafter Indian National Congress agreed in 1947 to the partition of the country because they wanted to avoid large scale civil war.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.9
questions.stem: It made its proposals in May. It still wanted a united India. There were to be a Federal Union composed of British provinces. The above quotation is related to
explanation: (D) ✓ — The Cabinet Mission: its proposals came in May 1946 and it "still wanted a united India" — CMP1946 was the only proposal where the British offered a united India & Purna Swaraj, a union built from the British provinces with a weak common centre.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — The Simon Commission reported in June 1930 and pointed to provincial autonomy with no change at the Centre — no May proposals for a federal union of provinces.
(B) ✗ — The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was a truce agreement of March 1931 — not a proposals document about a federal union.
(C) ✗ — Cripps came in March 1942 and leaned the other way: his secession clause threatened fragmentation into as many as 576 entities — not a Federal Union of provinces proposed in May.
(Note: The Cabinet Mission proposals came in May 1946, which opposed the demand of Pakistan and supported united India composed of British provinces.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.10
questions.stem: Which one of the following leaders of the Congress was totally in favour of Cabinet Mission plan?
explanation: (C) ✓ — Sardar Patel: he was "totally in favour of the Cabinet Mission Plan" — backing the Constituent Assembly and the interim-government framework it created.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — No total endorsement by Gandhi is recorded; the full-support credit belongs to Patel.
(B) ✗ — Nehru's July 1946 statement — that the only binding decision was the formation of a Constituent Assembly — is what gave ML1906 its excuse to reject the plan. Hardly 'totally in favour'.
(D) ✗ — No such total support is recorded for Azad; the recorded full supporter is Patel.

(Note: Sardar Patel of Congress was totally in favour of Cabinet Mission Plan. Patel favoured the Cabinet Mission proposals according to which with setting up of a constituent assembly and in an interim government.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.11
questions.stem: At the time of partition of India, which one of the following provinces of British India came forward with a plan for a united and independent existence?
explanation: (C) ✓ — Bengal. In April 1947, H.S. Suhrawardy (Bengal's Muslim League Chief Minister) and Sarat Bose proposed the United Bengal Plan — a sovereign, united Bengal independent of both India and Pakistan, with its own constitution and joint Muslim-Hindu electorates. The plan failed against opposition from both INC and ML1906.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Punjab's 1947 story ran the opposite way: its INC-Akali-Unionist coalition was overthrown by ML-led direct action; the united-independence plan came from Bengal (see the ✓ entry above).
(B) ✗ — Assam's recorded 1946–47 question was Sylhet and the compulsory Section C grouping — no independence plan; the plan in question was Bengal's.
(D) ✗ — Bihar, a Section A Hindu-majority province, produced no such plan; the United Bengal Plan is the basis of this answer (✓ entry above).

(Note: During the time of partition of India, Punjab province came forward with a plan for a united and independent existence, but it was due to the effort of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel that PEPSU came into existence.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.12
questions.stem: The Balkan Plan for fragmentation of India was the brainchild of
explanation: (C) ✓ — The plan was by Mountbatten — 'Dickie' was Mountbatten's nickname; Ismay was a member of his committee. The fragmentation blueprint was the new Viceroy's own brainchild — Nehru shot it down as 'balkanization' of India.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Churchill had been out of office since July 1945, when Clement Atlee had become British PM after Churchill lost the elections — the April 1947 plan came from the Viceroy's office.
(B) ✗ — Jinnah's recorded instrument of pressure was Direct Action; Plan Balkan was drafted under Mountbatten.
(D) ✗ — V.P. Menon's recorded role is Secretary of the States Department in the integration of the Princely States; the Balkan plan is credited to Mountbatten.
(Note: 'Balkan Plan' was the brainchild of Lord Mountbatten. He was authorised by British Government to resolve the situation in India.
Mountbatten soon concluded that transfer of power to one central representative authority was not feasible.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.13
questions.stem: As an alternative to the partition of India, Gandhiji suggested to Mountbatten that he

options.text: invited Jinnah to form the government
invited Nehru and Jinnah to form the government together
invite the army to take over for some time

explanation: (B) ✓ — Gandhi suggested to Mountbatten that Jinnah be invited to form the government as the alternative to partition — a move bitterly criticised by Congress members. It fits the recorded picture of Gandhi's lone fight against partition: by mid-1947 he was Mountbatten's "one-man boundary force".
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — No postponement suggestion is recorded — the Atlee deadline stood; Gandhi's recorded counter-move was the Jinnah-government idea.
(C) ✗ — The recorded suggestion was Jinnah alone forming the government — that was its whole point as an alternative to dividing the country.
(D) ✗ — An army take-over is recorded nowhere and is alien to Gandhi's recorded politics — his counsel was "don't accept partition in your hearts".
(Note: Gandhiji suggested to Mountbatten that he should invite Jinnah to form the government as alternative to the partition of India, but this move was bitterly criticised by the Congress members.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.14
questions.stem: The members of the Constituent Assembly which drafted the Constitution of India were

options.text: elected by the Legislative Assemblies of various province
elected by the Indian National Congress Muslim League

explanation: (C) ✓ — Proposals: the constitution was to be framed by a Constituent Assembly consisting of nominees of the Princely States & elected members from the PLAs — i.e. elected by the Legislative Assemblies of the provinces.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — The British Parliament nominated no one — its very jurisdiction over British India ended on the appointed day; the CA came from PLA elections.
(B) ✗ — The Governor General nominated no CA members; only the Princely States sent nominees, while provincial members were elected by the PLAs.
(D) ✗ — INC and ML contested the seats, but the electing bodies were the Provincial Legislative Assemblies — parties do not elect, legislatures did.

(Note: According to the Cabinet Mission proposal, the members of the Constituent Assembly which drafted the Constitution of India were elected by the legislative assemblies of various provinces with a proportional representation.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.15
questions.stem: President of Indian National Congress at the time of partition of India was
explanation: (B) ✓ — J.B. Kripalani: he served as Congress President from December 1946 to December 1947 — the chair at the moment of partition.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Rajagopalachari's recorded mark on this period is the 1944 formula; the 1947 presidency was Kripalani's.
(C) ✗ — Nehru was heading the Interim Government as Prime Minister from September 1946 — the government, not the party.
(D) ✗ — Azad's presidency ran till 1946, when Kripalani succeeded him.
(Note: At the time of partition of India, the Congress President was JB Kripalani from December, 1946 to December, 1947.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.16
questions.stem: The last opportunity to avoid the partition of India was
explanation: (C) ✓ — The Cabinet Mission was the last constitutional scheme for one India: CMP1946 was the only proposal where the British offered a united India & Purna Swaraj. When its grouping clause collapsed in rival interpretations and ML1906 called Direct Action, "the last effort to avoid partition was lost".
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Cripps (1942) still had the Wavell Plan and the Cabinet Mission ahead of it — and its own secession clause leaned toward fragmentation — so it was not the last chance.
(B) ✗ — The Rajaji Formula failed in the Gandhi-Jinnah talks of 1944 — two more schemes followed it; not the last opportunity.
(D) ✗ — The Wavell Plan collapsed in 1945 over ML1906's monopoly demand on Muslim seats — but the Cabinet Mission came after it, so Wavell was not the final chance.
(Note: Muslim League got 73 out of 78 seats in the interim government election based on Cabinet Plan, but Muslim League rejected the plan and thus the last effort to avoid partition was lost.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.17
questions.stem: Who headed the Interim Cabinet formed in the year 1946?
explanation: (B) ✓ — Proposals: Immediate transfer of executive power to an interim government at the Centre. (This was done in September 1946, with J.L. Nehru as Prime Minister.) Nehru headed the Interim Cabinet — with 12 ministers.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Rajendra Prasad's recorded 1946 office is the permanent Presidency of the Constituent Assembly, from 11 December 1946 — not the Interim Cabinet.
(C) ✗ — Patel's recorded leadership was of the States Department (with V.P. Menon) in the integration of the Princely States; in the Interim Cabinet he held Home — the head was Nehru.
(D) ✗ — Rajagopalachari is recorded for his 1944 formula; the Interim Cabinet of September 1946 was headed by Nehru.

(Note: The Interim Cabinet formed on 2nd September, 1946, as per Cabinet Mission proposal was headed by Jawaharlal Nehru with 12 Ministers. It had the task of assisting the transition of India and Pakistan from British rule.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.18
questions.stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the relations between India and Pakistan
1. During Shimla Agreement, Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Bhutto agreed to maintain the sanctity of LOC.
2. Lahore summit took place in the year 1997.
3. Islamabad summit was held between Rajiv Gandhi and Nawaz Sharif.
Which of these statement(s) is/are correct?
explanation: (D) ✓ — Only statement 1 holds: at Shimla, Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto agreed to maintain the sanctity of the LoC. The Lahore summit did not take place in 1997, and the Islamabad summit paired Rajiv Gandhi with Benazir Bhutto — not Nawaz Sharif. Hence only 1.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Overcounts: statements 2 and 3 both fail — wrong year for Lahore, wrong pairing for Islamabad.
(B) ✗ — Statement 3's pairing is wrong — Rajiv Gandhi met Benazir Bhutto at Islamabad, not Nawaz Sharif — so '1 and 3' fails.
(C) ✗ — Keeps both false statements and drops the true one: only the Shimla-Agreement statement survives the record.
(Note: Lahore summit took place in 1998 not in 1997. Islamabad summit was held between Rajiv Gandhi and Benazir Bhutto not with Nawaz Sharif. Hence, only statement one is correct.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.19
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The Constituent Assembly of India was elected by the Provincial Assemblies in the year 1946
Jawaharlal Nehru, MA Jinnah and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel were members of the Constituent Assembly of India
The First Session of the Constituent Assembly of India was held in January, 1947
The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th January, 1950

explanation: (A) ✓ — Statement (a) is correct: the Constituent Assembly was elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies in 1946 — "elected members from the PLAs" plus Princely-State nominees.
Wrong options:
(B) ✗ — Jinnah never sat in the Constituent Assembly: ML1906 refused to join it and by February 1947 was demanding its dissolution.
(C) ✗ — The first session was not in January 1947: The Constituent Assembly convened on 9 December 1946 with Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha as its Provisional President.
(D) ✗ — Confuses adoption with commencement: the Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950.
(Note: The Constituent Assembly of India was elected by the Provincial Assemblies in the year 1946 is correct.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.20
questions.stem: Assertion (A) According to the Wavell Plan, the number of Hindu and Muslim members in the Executive Council were to be equal. Reason (R) Wavell thought that this arrangement would have avoided the partition of India.

options.text: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: (C) ✓ — A is true: under the Wavell Plan 50% of Indian ministers would be Hindus & 50% would be Muslims. R is false: the recorded driver was British domestic politics — Winston Churchill wanted some visible progress on the India problem before elections in Britain — not a design to avert partition. Hence A true, R false.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Treats R as true, but no partition-avoidance motive is recorded for the parity clause — the Plan simply built on the Desai-Liaqat parity already agreed, timed to Britain's elections.
(B) ✗ — Also treats R as true; it fails the same way — the record recorded motive is electoral timing in Britain, not a theory that parity would avert partition.
(D) ✗ — A is not false: the Hindu-Muslim parity provision is recorded verbatim in the Plan's proposals.

(Note: Plan proposed by Wavell in Simla conference held in 1945, is called Wavel Plan. Under this plan, India was to be granted Dominion status in the near future. The Indians would themselves draft the Constitution.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.21
questions.stem: After Quit India Movement, C Rajagopalachari issued a pamphlet entitled 'The Way Out'. Which one of the following was a proposal in this pamphlet?

options.text: The establishment of a 'War Advisory Council' composed of representatives of British India and the Indian states
Reconstitution of the Central Executive Council in such a way that all its members, except the governor-general and the commander-in-chief should be Indian leaders
Fresh elections to the Central and Provincial Legislatures to be held at the end of 1945 and the Constitution making body to be convened as soon as possible
A solution for the constitutional deadlock

explanation: (D) ✓ — 'The Way Out' was Rajaji's pamphlet offering a route past the constitutional deadlock — the same impulse as his 1944 formula, "evolved with the 'Full' approval of Gandhiji" to break the INC-ML stalemate.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — A 'War Advisory Council' belongs to the August Offer of 1940 — not to Rajaji's pamphlet.
(B) ✗ — An all-Indian Executive Council except the GG and C-i-C is the Desai-Liaqat Pact / Wavell Plan structure — not the pamphlet's proposal.
(C) ✗ — Fresh elections at the end of 1945 plus a constitution-making body describes the Wavell-era sequence — the December 1945 PLA elections — not Rajaji's pamphlet.

(Note: In March 1944, Mr C Rajagopalachari evolved a formula with the 'Full' approval of Gandhiji for the Congress. The scheme embodying the formula was (i) The league would endorse the demand for independence.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.22
questions.stem: The Radcliffe Committee was appointed to

options.text: solve the problem of minorities in India
give effect to the Independence Bill
delimit the boundaries between India and Pakistan
enquire into the riots in East Bengal

explanation: (C) ✓ — Two boundary commissions were set up to demarcate borders in the west (Punjab) and the east (Bengal). Both were headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, a British jurist who had never been to India. The Radcliffe Committee's task was delimiting the India-Pakistan boundary.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — Minorities' rights were the subject of CMP1946's advisory committee; Radcliffe's commissions dealt with borders, with four partisan judges deadlocked over lines, not minorities.
(B) ✗ — Giving legal effect to independence was the Indian Independence Act's own work; the boundary commission was a distinct body for demarcation under it.
(D) ✗ — No riot-enquiry role is recorded; the commissions' sole recorded task was demarcating the western and eastern boundaries.
(Note: The Radcliffe Committee was created in July 1947 to delimit the boundaries between India and Pakistan, shortly before these nations were to become independent from Britain.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.23
questions.stem: With reference to the Cabinet Mission, which of the following statements is/are correct?
items: 1. It recommended a Federal Government.
2. It enlarged the powers of the Indian courts.
3. It provided for more Indians in the ICS.
questions.stemTail: Select the correct answer using the code given below :
explanation: (A) ✓ — Statement 1 is recorded: CMP1946 proposed a weak common centre handling only three union subjects... All other subjects & residual powers would be with the provinces — a federal (indeed confederal) government. Statements 2 and 3 — court powers and ICS Indianisation — appear nowhere among the recorded proposals. Hence only 1.
Wrong options:
(B) ✗ — Neither enlarged court powers nor more Indians in the ICS figures among the twelve recorded CMP proposals.
(C) ✗ — Statement 1 stands, but statement 3 fails — ICS recruitment is absent from the plan's recorded provisions.
(D) ✗ — Statement 1 is exactly the recorded structure — a weak common centre with three union subjects and residual powers to the provinces — so 'none' fails.

(Note: The Cabinet Mission arrived on March 24, 1946. The objective of this mission was to devise a machinery to draw up the constitution of Independent India and make arrangements for Interim Government.)

questions.label: PYQ_Pre.24
questions.stem: Who was the Provisional President of the Constituent Assembly before Dr. Rajendra Prasad took over?
explanation: (D) ✓ — Constituent Assembly: The Constituent Assembly convened on 9 December 1946 with Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha as its Provisional President. Two days later, on 11 December 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President.
Wrong options:
(A) ✗ — No Constituent-Assembly chair is recorded for Rajagopalachari; the provisional presidency was Dr Sachchidananda Sinha's.
(B) ✗ — Ambedkar's recorded CA fact here is his West Bengal seat (PYQ_Pre.4 above) — the provisional presidency belonged to Dr Sinha.
(C) ✗ — T.T. Krishnamachari is not recorded in this role; the Assembly opened under Dr Sachchidananda Sinha before Rajendra Prasad's election.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_1
questions.stem: Under the Rajaji Formula (1944), what was proposed to be held in Muslim-majority regions after the war?

options.text: A plebiscite on the question of partition
Direct elections to Provincial Legislative Assemblies
A constituent assembly for the Muslim Quam

explanation: Why others wrong: (b) Separate electorates were Jinnah's counter-demand for voting, not the original proposal — Chapter. (c) PLA elections happened in December 1945 under a separate process — Chapter. (d) The Muslim Quam framing belongs to Syed Ahmed Khan / 14-Point demands — Chapter; the formula proposed a plebiscite, not a separate CA.
Memory hook: Rajaji's three planks: Swaraj, coalition, plebiscite — "vote, then maybe partition."

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_2
questions.stem: Who negotiated the Desai-Liaqat Pact (1945) on behalf of the INC and the ML1906 in the Central Legislative Assembly?

options.text: Bullabhai Desai and Liaqat Ali Khan
J.L. Nehru and Liaqat Ali Khan
Maulana Azad and Liaqat Ali Khan

explanation: Why others wrong: (a) Rajagopalachari and Jinnah are the Rajaji Formula talks of 1944 — Chapter -2. (c) Nehru led the Interim Government from September 1946; not a CLA negotiator for this pact — Chapter. (d) Maulana Azad was INC President but not the CLA negotiator named in Chapter.
Memory hook: Desai-Liaqat = the two CLA floor leaders, not the top brass.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_3
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Wavell Plan (1945):
items: 1. It proposed parity between Hindus and Muslims in the Viceroy's Executive Council.
2. The Governor General and the Commander-in-Chief were the only non-Indian members proposed.
3. ML1906 demanded that all Muslim ministers come exclusively from ML1906.
4. Wavell announced that INC was responsible for the plan's failure.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 4 is incorrect: Wavell announced that ML1906 could not be convinced — i.e. he placed responsibility on ML1906, not INC. Statements 1, 2, 3 are directly in and. Hence (a), (c), (d) all carry a wrong combination.
Memory hook: Wavell parity, two whites (GG + C-i-C), ML's monopoly demand, blame on ML — three rights, one wrong.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_4
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about the composition of the Cabinet Mission (1946) is correct?

options.text: It was led by Lord Mountbatten and included Sir Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander
Its three members were Lord Wavell, Sir Stafford Cripps and Lord Pethick-Lawrence
Its three members were Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander
Its three members were Lord Pethick-Lawrence, A.V. Alexander and Lord Ismay

explanation: Why others wrong: (a) Mountbatten replaced Wavell only later under the Atlee Statement of February 1947 — Chapter; he was not a Cabinet Mission member. (b) Wavell was Viceroy, not a Cabinet Mission member — Chapter. (d) Ismay was a member of Mountbatten's committee for the Plan Balkan, not the Cabinet Mission — Chapter.
Memory hook: PLA — Pethick-Lawrence, Lord-of-Trade Cripps, Admiralty's Alexander.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_5
questions.stem: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946), which three subjects were to be handled by the proposed weak common centre?
explanation: Why others wrong: (a) Finance was retained by ML1906 in the Interim Government later to obstruct functioning — Chapter; it was not a Union subject under CMP1946. (c) Currency is not listed in. (d) Internal Security is not among the three Union subjects in; residual powers were with provinces.
Memory hook: DCF — Defence, Communications, Foreign — the only three at the weak centre.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_6
questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the grouping of provinces under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946):
items: 1. Section A was to frame a group constitution covering Defence and Foreign Affairs.
2. Section B grouped the Muslim-majority provinces of the west: NWFP, Punjab and Sindh.
3. Assam was placed in Section C even though it was not a Muslim-majority province.
4. After general elections, a province could come out of its group.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 1 is incorrect: Section A was indeed the Hindu-majority group, but Defence, Communications and Foreign Affairs were the three UNION subjects kept with the weak common centre. Each section framed its group constitution for all subjects EXCEPT these three. Statement 2 is correct: Section B = the Muslim-majority provinces of the west — NWFP, Punjab and Sindh. Statement 3 is correct: Assam (only 31% Muslim) was placed in Section C because Sylhet district had a Muslim majority. Statement 4 is correct: after general elections a province could come out of its group, so a group constitution was not permanently binding. (a) 1 and 2 only, (b) 1, 2 and 3 only and (d) 1, 2, 3 and 4 all carry the defective statement 1 and therefore fall.

Memory hook: Memory hook: A-Hindu, B-NW-Muslim, C-East-with-Assam, leave-after-elections — but the sections framed EVERYTHING EXCEPT Defence, Communications, Foreign Affairs; those three stayed with the Centre.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_7
questions.stem: The Direct Action Day was called by the ML1906 to be observed on which date, and led to communal riots in which city?
explanation: Why others wrong: (b) 14 August 1947 is one day before the appointed day of independence — Chapter; not Direct Action Day. (c) 9 August is associated with the Quit India Movement launch; the Naval Mutiny was the Bombay event of 1946 — Chapter. (d) 26 January is the date the Indian Constitution came into effect — Chapter / 10.7 closing line.
Memory hook: 16-Aug-46, Calcutta — 5,000 dead in a single week.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_8
questions.stem: Which one of the following correctly describes the Atlee Statement of February 1947?

options.text: Promised a constituent assembly elected on universal adult franchise
Set 30 June 1948 as the deadline for British withdrawal and named Mountbatten to replace Wavell
Declared that Britain would transfer power to one united India only
Promised dominion status with continued British paramountcy over Princely States

explanation: Why others wrong: (a) The Atlee Statement did not set up a new constituent assembly on adult franchise — the CA had already convened on 9 December 1946. (c) The Atlee Statement was pro-balkanisation: power could go to the Interim Government and to provinces that had not joined the CA. (d) Paramountcy over the 565 Princely States was to lapse, not continue.
Memory hook: Atlee's two bombs — June-1948 deadline + MTB-replaces-Wavell.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_9
questions.stem: The Plan Balkan / Ismay Plan / Dickie Bird Plan (April 1947) was opposed and effectively shelved chiefly because:

options.text: Jinnah refused to accept dominion status for Pakistan
The Princely States demanded merger before any plan was tabled
Nehru opposed it as it proposed transferring power to 11 provinces separately
The British Parliament rejected it as inconsistent with the Cabinet Mission Plan

explanation: Why others wrong: (a) Jinnah's reaction is not the reason cited in Chapter. (b) The Princely States question is dealt with in and is not the trigger for shelving Plan Balkan. (d) Chapter attributes the shelving to Nehru's opposition; no British Parliament rejection is recorded.
Memory hook: Dickie's USA-style "11 separate provinces" — Nehru's "balkanisation!" killed it.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_10
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the 3rd June Plan / Mountbatten Plan (1947):
items: 1. It granted dominion status to both India and Pakistan.
2. It advanced the date of British withdrawal to 15 August
3. It provided for partition decision in Punjab and Bengal by a simple majority of either Hindu or Muslim members of the Provincial Legislative Assemblies.
4. It provided for a plebiscite in NWFP.
questions.stemTail: 1947 Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 4 is incorrect — Chapter specifies a referendum (binding) in NWFP and Sylhet, not a plebiscite (non-binding); plebiscite was used for Sindh. Statements 1, 2, 3 are in, and respectively. Hence (b), (c), (d) all carry a wrong combination.
Memory hook: Dominion + 15-Aug + simple-majority PLAs — but NWFP got referendum, not plebiscite.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_11
questions.stem: Under the Mountbatten Plan (1947), which method of ascertaining popular will was used in each of the following regions?
items: 1. Sindh
2. NWFP and Sylhet district of Assam
3. Baluchistan
questions.stemTail: Which of the following correctly matches each region with the method used?
explanation: Why others wrong: the actual methods were (i) Plebiscite in Sindh, (ii) Referendum in NWFP and Sylhet, (iii) Voting by political leaders in Baluchistan. Options (a), (b), (c) each swap at least two of these methods.
Memory hook: Plebiscite-Sindh, Referendum-NWFP/Sylhet, Vote-of-leaders-Baluchistan — three regions, three methods.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_12
questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of provinces or regions voted to join Pakistan following the Mountbatten Plan (1947)?

options.text: NWFP, Punjab, Sindh and Assam (entire province)
Bengal (entire province), NWFP, Sindh and Baluchistan

explanation: Why others wrong: (b) Only Sylhet district of Assam, not the entire province of Assam, voted to join Pakistan — Chapter. (c) Bengal was partitioned, not transferred whole — Chapter / 8.4. (d) Hyderabad was integrated into India by Operation Polo in September 1948 — Chapter.
Memory hook: Four to Pakistan: NWFP + Sindh + Baluchistan + Sylhet.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_13
questions.stem: With reference to the Boundary Commission set up under the Mountbatten Plan (1947), consider the following statements:
items: 1. Two boundary commissions were set up — one for Punjab and one for Bengal.
2. Both were headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe.
3. The Radcliffe Line was announced on 15 August 1947, the appointed day.
4. Each commission had four judges nominated jointly by INC and ML1906.
questions.stemTail: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 3 is incorrect — the Radcliffe Line was announced on 17 August 1947, two days after independence. Statement 4 is incorrect — each commission had four judges, but two were nominated by INC and two by ML1906 (not jointly). Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hence (b), (c), (d) are wrong.
Memory hook: Two commissions, one Radcliffe, lines on 17-Aug — maximum chaos by design.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_14
questions.stem: Of the 565 officially recognised Princely States at the time of British withdrawal, how many ultimately acceded to the Dominion of India?
explanation: Why others wrong: (a) 549 is the number that signed the Instrument of Accession by or shortly after 15 August 1947, before J&K, Junagadh and Hyderabad were integrated — Chapter. (c) 562 is the widely repeated factual error traceable to the Butler Committee Report (1927) — Chapter Note on Numbers. (d) 565 was the total; 13 of these acceded to Pakistan — Chapter.
Memory hook: 565 total = 552 India (549 + 3) + 13 Pakistan; 562 is the internet's wrong answer.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_15
questions.stem: Which one of the following Princely States was integrated into the Indian Union through a military operation known as "Operation Polo"?
explanation: Why others wrong: (a) J&K acceded to India in October 1947 after an invasion by Pakistani-backed tribal militias — Chapter. (b) Junagadh was integrated in February 1948 through a public plebiscite — Chapter. (d) Bahawalpur was one of the 13 Princely States that acceded to the Dominion of Pakistan — Chapter.
Memory hook: Polo for Hyderabad, plebiscite for Junagadh, tribal-invasion for J&K — three holdouts, three routes.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_16
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the Indian Independence Act (July 1947):
items: 1. It partitioned British India into two independent dominions on the appointed day of 15 August
2. The same Governor General would serve both dominions until their respective Constituent Assemblies passed a law for a separate Governor General.
3. The title "Emperor of India" was abolished.
4. The Government of India Act 1935 was to apply until the passage of a new constitution.
questions.stemTail: 1947 Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Why others wrong: Statement 1 is in; statement 2 is in; statement 3 is in; statement 4 is in. All four are correct verbatim from Chapter; (a), (b), (c) each omit a correct statement.
Memory hook: Two dominions, one GG (briefly), no Emperor, GoI-1935 as bridge — Independence Act in one breath.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_17
questions.stem: Arrange the following events in correct chronological order:
items: 1. Rajaji Formula proposed
2. Desai-Liaqat Pact
3. Wavell Plan / Simla Conference
4. Arrival of the Cabinet Mission in India
explanation: Why others wrong: Chapter dates: Rajaji Formula = 1944; Desai-Liaqat Pact = 1945 — finalised before the Wavell Plan and used as the latter's basis; Wavell Plan discussed at Simla in June 1945; Cabinet Mission arrived in February 1946. Hence the order is 1-2-3-4; (a), (b), (d) misplace at least one event.

questions.label: FYQ_Pre_18
questions.stem: Arrange the following events of 1946–47 in correct chronological order:
items: 1. Direct Action Day
2. Constituent Assembly convened with Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha as Provisional President
3. Atlee Statement announcing 30 June 1948 deadline
4. 3rd June Plan / Mountbatten Plan
explanation: Why others wrong: Chapter dates: Direct Action Day = 16 August 1946; Constituent Assembly convened on 9 December 1946; Atlee Statement = February 1947; 3rd June Plan = 3 June 1947. Order is 1-2-3-4; (a), (b), (d) misplace at least one event.
